   140→from typing import List, Tuple, Dict, Callable
   141→
   142→_ALWD = set(":;,.0123456789")
   143→
   144→# ---------------- core parsing helpers ----------------
   145→
   146→def _find_bar(s: str) -> int:
   147→    com = False
   148→    for i, ch in enumerate(s):
   149→        if ch in ('\n', '\r'):
   150→            com = False
   151→        elif ch == '#':
   152→            com = True
   153→        elif ch == '|' and not com:
   154→            return i
   155→    return -1
   156→
   157→def _spans(text: str) -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
   158→    res, com, in_tok, st = [], False, False, 0
   159→    for i, ch in enumerate(text):
   160→        if ch in ('\n', '\r'):
   161→            if in_tok: res.append((st, i)); in_tok = False
   162→            com = False
   163→        elif ch == '#':
   164→            if in_tok: res.append((st, i)); in_tok = False
   165→            com = True
   166→        elif not com:
   167→            if ch in _ALWD:
   168→                if not in_tok: in_tok, st = True, i
   169→            else:
   170→                if in_tok: res.append((st, i)); in_tok = False
   171→    if in_tok: res.append((st, len(text)))
   172→    return res
   173→
   174→def _choose_sep(text: str, spans: List[Tuple[int, int]]) -> str:
   175→    if len(spans) >= 2:
   176→        a, b = spans[-2][1], spans[-1][0]
   177→        return '\n' if ('\n' in text[a:b] or '\r' in text[a:b]) else ' '
   178→    return '\n' if ('\n' in text or '\r' in text) else ' '
   179→
   180→def _ends_in_comment_line(text: str) -> bool:
   181→    ln = text.rfind('\n')
   182→    seg = text[ln + 1:] if ln != -1 else text
   183→    return '#' in seg
   184→
   185→def _append_tokens(text: str, k: int, sep: str) -> str:
   186→    if k <= 0: return text
   187→    t = text
   188→    if _ends_in_comment_line(t) and (not t.endswith('\n')): t += '\n'
   189→    parts = []
   190→    if t and not t[-1].isspace(): parts.append(sep)
   191→    parts.append('1')
   192→    for _ in range(k - 1):
   193→        parts.append(sep); parts.append('1')
   194→    return t + ''.join(parts)
   195→
   196→def _erase_span_and_one_sep(text: str, st: int, en: int) -> str:
   197→    n = len(text)
   198→    r = en
   199→    while r < n and text[r] in (' ', '\t'): r += 1
   200→    if r > en: return text[:st] + text[r:]
   201→    l = st
   202→    while l > 0 and text[l-1] in (' ', '\t'): l -= 1
   203→    if l < st: return text[:l] + text[en:]
   204→    return text[:st] + text[en:]
   205→
   206→def _trim_last_tokens(text: str, spans: List[Tuple[int, int]], drop: int) -> str:
   207→    if drop <= 0: return text
   208→    new_text = text
   209→    for st, en in reversed(spans[-drop:]):
   210→        new_text = _erase_span_and_one_sep(new_text, st, en)
   211→    while new_text and new_text[-1] in (' ', '\t'):
   212→        new_text = new_text[:-1]
   213→    return new_text
   214→
   215→def _enforce_count(text: str, target: int) -> str:
   216→    sp = _spans(text); cur = len(sp)
   217→    if cur == target: return text
   218→    if cur > target:  return _trim_last_tokens(text, sp, cur - target)
   219→    sep = _choose_sep(text, sp)
   220→    return _append_tokens(text, target - cur, sep)
   221→
   222→def _strip_bars_outside_comments(s: str) -> str:
   223→    com, out = False, []
   224→    for ch in s:
   225→        if ch in ('\n', '\r'): com = False; out.append(ch)
   226→        elif ch == '#':        com = True;  out.append(ch)
   227→        elif ch == '|' and not com: continue
   228→        else: out.append(ch)
   229→    return ''.join(out)
   230→
   231→def _replace_tokens(text: str, repl: Dict[int, str]) -> str:
   232→    if not repl: return text
   233→    sp = _spans(text)
   234→    for idx in sorted(repl.keys(), reverse=True):
   235→        if 0 <= idx < len(sp):
   236→            st, en = sp[idx]
   237→            text = text[:st] + repl[idx] + text[en:]
   238→    return text
   239→
   240→def _drop_tokens_by_indices(text: str, idxs: List[int]) -> str:
   241→    if not idxs: return text
   242→    out = text
   243→    for idx in sorted(set(idxs), reverse=True):
   244→        sp = _spans(out)  # recompute spans after each deletion
   245→        if 0 <= idx < len(sp):
   246→            st, en = sp[idx]
   247→            out = _erase_span_and_one_sep(out, st, en)
   248→    return out
   249→
   250→# ---------------- identity for dedupe ----------------
   251→
   252→def _default_path_key(p: str) -> str:
   253→    s = p.strip().replace('\\', '/')
   254→    while '//' in s: s = s.replace('//', '/')
   255→    if len(s) > 1 and s.endswith('/'): s = s[:-1]
   256→    return s
   257→
   258→# ---------------- new-set splitter (FIX) ----------------
   259→
   260→def _select_new_side(
   261→    loras_new: List[str],
   262→    mult_new: str,
   263→    mode: str,  # "merge before" | "merge after"
   264→) -> Tuple[List[str], str]:
   265→    """
   266→    Split mult_new on '|' (outside comments) and split loras_new accordingly.
   267→    Return ONLY the side relevant to `mode`. Extras loras (if any) are appended to the selected side.
   268→    """
   269→    bi = _find_bar(mult_new)
   270→    if bi == -1:
   271→        return loras_new, _strip_bars_outside_comments(mult_new)
   272→
   273→    left, right = mult_new[:bi], mult_new[bi + 1:]
   274→    nL, nR = len(_spans(left)), len(_spans(right))
   275→    L = len(loras_new)
   276→
   277→    # Primary allocation by token counts
   278→    b_count = min(nL, L)
   279→    rem     = max(0, L - b_count)
   280→    a_count = min(nR, rem)
   281→    extras  = max(0, L - (b_count + a_count))
   282→
   283→    if mode == "merge before":
   284→        # take BEFORE loras + extras
   285→        l_sel = loras_new[:b_count] + (loras_new[b_count + a_count : b_count + a_count + extras] if extras else [])
   286→        m_sel = left
   287→    else:
   288→        # take AFTER loras + extras
   289→        start_after = b_count
   290→        l_sel = loras_new[start_after:start_after + a_count] + (loras_new[start_after + a_count : start_after + a_count + extras] if extras else [])
   291→        m_sel = right
   292→
   293→    return l_sel, _strip_bars_outside_comments(m_sel)

   297→def merge_loras_settings(
   298→    loras_old: List[str],
   299→    mult_old: str,
   300→    loras_new: List[str],
   301→    mult_new: str,
   302→    mode: str = "merge before",
   303→    path_key: Callable[[str], str] = _default_path_key,
   304→) -> Tuple[List[str], str]:
   305→    """
   306→    Merge settings with full formatting/comment preservation and correct handling of `mult_new` with '|'.
   307→    Dedup rule: when merging AFTER (resp. BEFORE), if a new lora already exists in preserved BEFORE (resp. AFTER),
   308→    update that preserved multiplier and drop the duplicate from the replaced side.
   309→    """
   310→    assert mode in ("merge before", "merge after")
   311→    mult_old= mult_old.strip()
   312→    mult_new= mult_new.strip()
   313→
   314→    # Old split & alignment
   315→    bi_old = _find_bar(mult_old)
   316→    before_old, after_old = (mult_old[:bi_old], mult_old[bi_old + 1:]) if bi_old != -1 else ("", mult_old)
   317→    orig_had_bar = (bi_old != -1)
   318→
   319→    sp_b_old, sp_a_old = _spans(before_old), _spans(after_old)
   320→    n_b_old = len(sp_b_old)
   321→    total_old = len(loras_old)
   322→
   323→    if n_b_old <= total_old:
   324→        keep_b = n_b_old
   325→        keep_a = total_old - keep_b
   326→        before_old_aligned = before_old
   327→        after_old_aligned  = _enforce_count(after_old, keep_a)
   328→    else:
   329→        keep_b = total_old
   330→        keep_a = 0
   331→        before_old_aligned = _enforce_count(before_old, keep_b)
   332→        after_old_aligned  = _enforce_count(after_old, 0)
   333→
   334→    # NEW: choose the relevant side of the *new* set (fix for '|' in mult_new)
   335→    loras_new_sel, mult_new_sel = _select_new_side(loras_new, mult_new, mode)
   336→    mult_new_aligned = _enforce_count(mult_new_sel, len(loras_new_sel))
   337→    sp_new = _spans(mult_new_aligned)
   338→    new_tokens = [mult_new_aligned[st:en] for st, en in sp_new]
   339→
   340→    if mode == "merge after":
   341→        # Preserve BEFORE; replace AFTER (with dedupe/update)
   342→        preserved_loras = loras_old[:keep_b]
   343→        preserved_text  = before_old_aligned
   344→        preserved_spans = _spans(preserved_text)
   345→        pos_by_key: Dict[str, int] = {}
   346→        for i, lp in enumerate(preserved_loras):
   347→            k = path_key(lp)
   348→            if k not in pos_by_key: pos_by_key[k] = i
   349→
   350→        repl_map: Dict[int, str] = {}
   351→        drop_idxs: List[int] = []
   352→        for i, lp in enumerate(loras_new_sel):
   353→            j = pos_by_key.get(path_key(lp))
   354→            if j is not None and j < len(preserved_spans):
   355→                repl_map[j] = new_tokens[i] if i < len(new_tokens) else "1"
   356→                drop_idxs.append(i)
   357→
   358→        before_text = _replace_tokens(preserved_text, repl_map)
   359→        after_text  = _drop_tokens_by_indices(mult_new_aligned, drop_idxs)
   360→        loras_keep  = [lp for i, lp in enumerate(loras_new_sel) if i not in set(drop_idxs)]
   361→        loras_out   = preserved_loras + loras_keep
   362→
   363→    else:
   364→        # Preserve AFTER; replace BEFORE (with dedupe/update)
   365→        preserved_loras = loras_old[keep_b:]
   366→        preserved_text  = after_old_aligned
   367→        preserved_spans = _spans(preserved_text)
   368→        pos_by_key: Dict[str, int] = {}
   369→        for i, lp in enumerate(preserved_loras):
   370→            k = path_key(lp)
   371→            if k not in pos_by_key: pos_by_key[k] = i
   372→
   373→        repl_map: Dict[int, str] = {}
   374→        drop_idxs: List[int] = []
   375→        for i, lp in enumerate(loras_new_sel):
   376→            j = pos_by_key.get(path_key(lp))
   377→            if j is not None and j < len(preserved_spans):
   378→                repl_map[j] = new_tokens[i] if i < len(new_tokens) else "1"
   379→                drop_idxs.append(i)
   380→
   381→        after_text  = _replace_tokens(preserved_text, repl_map)
   382→        before_text = _drop_tokens_by_indices(mult_new_aligned, drop_idxs)
   383→        loras_keep  = [lp for i, lp in enumerate(loras_new_sel) if i not in set(drop_idxs)]
   384→        loras_out   = loras_keep + preserved_loras
   385→
   386→    # Compose, preserving explicit "before-only" bar when appropriate
   387→    has_before = len(_spans(before_text)) > 0
   388→    has_after  = len(_spans(after_text)) > 0
   389→    if has_before and has_after:
   390→        mult_out = f"{before_text}|{after_text}"
   391→    elif has_before:
   392→        mult_out = before_text + ('|' if (mode == 'merge before' or orig_had_bar) else '')
   393→    else:
   394→        mult_out = after_text
   395→
   396→    return loras_out, mult_out
   397→
   398→# ---------------- extractor ----------------
   399→
   400→def extract_loras_side(
   401→    loras: List[str],
   402→    mult: str,
   403→    which: str = "before",
   404→) -> Tuple[List[str], str]:
   405→    assert which in ("before", "after")
   406→    bi = _find_bar(mult)
   407→    before_txt, after_txt = (mult[:bi], mult[bi + 1:]) if bi != -1 else ("", mult)
   408→
   409→    sp_b = _spans(before_txt)
   410→    n_b  = len(sp_b)
   411→    total = len(loras)
   412→
   413→    if n_b <= total:
   414→        keep_b = n_b
   415→        keep_a = total - keep_b
   416→    else:
   417→        keep_b = total
   418→        keep_a = 0
   419→
   420→    if which == "before":
   421→        return loras[:keep_b], _enforce_count(before_txt, keep_b)
   422→    else:
   423→        return loras[keep_b:keep_b + keep_a], _enforce_count(after_txt, keep_a)
   424→

    12→def make_send_cmd() -> Callable:
    13→    """Create a send_cmd callback for WGP progress reporting."""
    14→
    15→    def send_cmd(cmd: str, data=None):
    16→        if cmd == "status":
    17→            generation_logger.debug(f"Status: {data}")
    18→        elif cmd == "progress":
    19→            if isinstance(data, list) and len(data) >= 2:
    20→                progress, status = data[0], data[1]
    21→                generation_logger.debug(f"Progress: {progress}% - {status}")
    22→            else:
    23→                generation_logger.debug(f"Progress: {data}")
    24→        elif cmd == "output":
    25→            generation_logger.essential("Output generated")
    26→        elif cmd == "exit":
    27→            generation_logger.essential("Generation completed")
    28→        elif cmd == "error":
    29→            generation_logger.error(f"Error: {data}")
    30→        elif cmd == "info":
    31→            generation_logger.debug(f"Info: {data}")
    32→        elif cmd == "preview":
    33→            generation_logger.debug("Preview updated")
    34→
    35→    return send_cmd

Now I have the complete picture. Here is a comprehensive analysis:

---

## Analysis of Distill LoRA in the LTX2 Pipeline

### 1. What does `"0;1"` mean in `loras_multipliers`?

`"0;1"` is a **per-guidance-phase multiplier** for the distill LoRA. The `;` syntax in `parse_loras_multipliers` (see `/Wan2GP/shared/utils/loras_mutipliers.py` lines 69-95) splits the string on `;` to produce one value per guidance phase:

- `"0;1"` → phase 1 multiplier = `0.0`, phase 2 multiplier = `1.0`

For the LTX2 dev model, `guidance_phases` is locked to `2` (`guidance_max_phases: 2`, `lock_guidance_phases: True` per `ltx2_handler.py` lines 228-230). So the distill LoRA is **disabled in phase 1** (the high-noise denoising phase) and **enabled at full strength in phase 2** (the refinement phase). This is the standard two-stage dev pipeline behaviour — the distill LoRA is used as a phase-2 refinement prior only.

### 2. Does `ltx2_22B_distilled.json` define any loras?

No. The distilled model JSON has **no `loras` field at all**. It only sets `"ltx2_pipeline": "distilled"`. The distill LoRA is not needed for the distilled checkpoint because distillation is already baked into the weights. The `_ARCH_SPECS` in `ltx2_handler.py` (line 32) does keep a `distilled_lora` filename reference (`ltx-2.3-22b-distilled-lora-384.safetensors`), but the handler itself never auto-injects it — it is only listed in the model def JSON's `loras` field for the dev variant.

### 3. `task_conversion.py` param_whitelist — LoRA params

Yes, the whitelist (lines 50-51) includes all relevant LoRA params:

```python
"activated_loras", "loras_multipliers", "additional_loras", "loras",
```

So `activated_loras`, `loras_multipliers`, `additional_loras`, and `loras` all pass through from the task's DB params to the `GenerationTask.parameters` dict. They would then flow into the WGP call.

### 4. How WGP applies the model definition's `loras` — the critical mechanism

This is the heart of the answer. WGP's `generate_video` (in `wgp.py`) calls `get_transformer_loras(model_type)` (lines 5386-5393) **unconditionally at the start of every generation**, regardless of what the task passes in:

```python
def get_transformer_loras(model_type):
    model_def = get_model_def(model_type)
    transformer_loras_filenames = get_model_recursive_prop(model_type, "loras", return_list=True)
    lora_dir = get_lora_dir(model_type)
    transformer_loras_filenames = [ os.path.join(lora_dir, os.path.basename(filename)) for filename in transformer_loras_filenames]
    transformer_loras_multipliers = get_model_recursive_prop(model_type, "loras_multipliers", return_list=True) + [1.] * len(transformer_loras_filenames)
    transformer_loras_multipliers = transformer_loras_multipliers[:len(transformer_loras_filenames)]
    return transformer_loras_filenames, transformer_loras_multipliers
```

Then inside `generate_video` (lines 6012-6017):

```python
transformer_loras_filenames, transformer_loras_multipliers = get_transformer_loras(model_type)
if transformer_loras_filenames != None:
    loras_list_mult_choices_nums, loras_slists, errors = parse_loras_multipliers(
        transformer_loras_multipliers, len(transformer_loras_filenames), num_inference_steps,
        nb_phases=guidance_phases, model_switch_phase=model_switch_phase)
    loras_selected = transformer_loras_filenames
```

The transformer (model-def) LoRAs are **prepended to the LoRA stack**, and then user `activated_loras` (if any) are merged on top (lines 6025-6031). The transformer LoRAs are also stored in metadata (lines 7020-7024).

**Crucially**, `get_model_recursive_prop` reads from `models_def` which is populated by loading the model's JSON file (the `defaults/ltx2_22B.json`). This is per-model-type, not per-task.

### 5. Does `ltx2_pipeline: "distilled"` change how the distill LoRA is applied?

Yes, but indirectly. The distilled model JSON has **no `loras` field**, so `get_transformer_loras` returns an empty list for `ltx2_22B_distilled`. There is nothing to apply. The `ltx2_pipeline: "distilled"` flag also changes the `load_model` return value (line 382-383): for the distilled pipeline it does **not** include the `"loras": ["text_embedding_projection", "text_embeddings_connector"]` exclusion directive — meaning the distilled model loads slightly differently at the `pipe` level, but that's internal to model loading.

Also from `ltx2_handler.py` lines 204-210: the distilled pipeline sets `lock_inference_steps: True`, `no_negative_prompt: True`, and locks `guidance_phases` to `1` (line 450), removing the two-phase structure entirely.

### 6. The bottom line: does the caller need to pass LoRA params?

**No. For `model: "ltx2_22B"` (dev model), the distill LoRA is applied automatically by WGP from the model definition.** The flow is:

1. WGP loads `defaults/ltx2_22B.json` into `models_def["ltx2_22B"]`
2. At generation time, `get_transformer_loras("ltx2_22B")` reads `loras` from that def → finds `ltx-2.3-22b-distilled-lora-384.safetensors`
3. It reads `loras_multipliers` → finds `["0;1"]`
4. These become the "transformer LoRAs" (always-on baseline stack) — applied before any user LoRAs
5. With `guidance_phases=2` (locked), the `"0;1"` is parsed as phase1=0.0, phase2=1.0

For `model: "ltx2_22B_distilled"`, there are no model-def LoRAs — the distilled weights have it baked in.

### What this means for test cases

**Test cases do NOT need to include any LoRA-related params for the distill LoRA.** WGP handles it entirely from the model definition for `ltx2_22B`. The only time you'd need to pass LoRA params is if a test is explicitly testing user-specified LoRAs (via `activated_loras` + `loras_multipliers`) on top of the model baseline. The `param_resolution.py` does set `"activated_loras": []` and `"loras_multipliers": ""` as system defaults, which is correct — they'll be empty unless the task or model defaults supply them, and the model-def LoRAs go through a completely separate `get_transformer_loras()` code path in WGP that bypasses the `activated_loras` parameter entirely.

   109→def get_default_model(task_type: str) -> str:
   110→    """
   111→    Get the default model for a given task type.
   112→
   113→    Args:
   114→        task_type: The task type identifier
   115→
   116→    Returns:
   117→        The default model identifier, or "t2v" as fallback
   118→    """
   119→    return TASK_TYPE_TO_MODEL.get(task_type, "t2v")
   120→
   121→
   122→def is_wgp_task(task_type: str) -> bool:
   123→    """Check if a task type is a WGP generation task."""
   124→    return task_type in WGP_TASK_TYPES
   125→
   126→
   127→def is_direct_queue_task(task_type: str) -> bool:
   128→    """Check if a task type can be directly queued."""
   129→    return task_type in DIRECT_QUEUE_TASK_TYPES

1→"""WGP parameter dictionary builders.
     2→
     3→Constructs the keyword-argument dictionaries passed to wgp.generate_video()
     4→for both passthrough mode and normal mode.
     5→"""
     6→
     7→from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, Optional
     8→
     9→from source.core.log import generation_logger
    10→
    11→
    12→def make_send_cmd() -> Callable:
    13→    """Create a send_cmd callback for WGP progress reporting."""
    14→
    15→    def send_cmd(cmd: str, data=None):
    16→        if cmd == "status":
    17→            generation_logger.debug(f"Status: {data}")
    18→        elif cmd == "progress":
    19→            if isinstance(data, list) and len(data) >= 2:
    20→                progress, status = data[0], data[1]
    21→                generation_logger.debug(f"Progress: {progress}% - {status}")
    22→            else:
    23→                generation_logger.debug(f"Progress: {data}")
    24→        elif cmd == "output":
    25→            generation_logger.essential("Output generated")
    26→        elif cmd == "exit":
    27→            generation_logger.essential("Generation completed")
    28→        elif cmd == "error":
    29→            generation_logger.error(f"Error: {data}")
    30→        elif cmd == "info":
    31→            generation_logger.debug(f"Info: {data}")
    32→        elif cmd == "preview":
    33→            generation_logger.debug("Preview updated")
    34→
    35→    return send_cmd
    36→
    37→

    13→def db_task_to_generation_task(db_task_params: dict, task_id: str, task_type: str, wan2gp_path: str, debug_mode: bool = False) -> GenerationTask:
    14→    """
    15→    Convert a database task row to a GenerationTask object for the queue system.
    16→    """
    17→    headless_logger.debug(f"Converting DB task to GenerationTask", task_id=task_id)
    18→
    19→    prompt = db_task_params.get("prompt", "")
    20→
    21→    # For img2img tasks, empty prompt is acceptable (will use minimal changes)
    22→    # Provide a minimal default prompt to avoid errors
    23→    img2img_task_types = {"z_image_turbo_i2i", "qwen_image_edit", "qwen_image_style", "image_inpaint"}
    24→    if not prompt:
    25→        if task_type in img2img_task_types:
    26→            prompt = " "  # Minimal prompt for img2img
    27→            headless_logger.debug(f"Task {task_id}: Using minimal prompt for img2img task", task_id=task_id)
    28→        else:
    29→            raise ValueError(f"Task {task_id}: prompt is required")
    30→    
    31→    model = db_task_params.get("model")
    32→    if not model:
    33→        from source.task_handlers.tasks.task_types import get_default_model

   182→                    target_pixels = IMG2IMG_TARGET_MEGAPIXELS
   183→                    current_pixels = width * height
   184→

   188→                        scale = math.sqrt(target_pixels / current_pixels)

   195→                        scaled_width = (scaled_width // 8) * 8

   106→
   107→    def __init__(self, *streams: io.TextIOBase):
   108→        self._streams = streams

   114→            if enc:
   115→                return enc
   116→        return "utf-8"

   123→

   212→def load_case_definitions(manifest_path: Path = DEFAULT_MANIFEST_PATH) -> list[CaseDefinition]:
   213→    payload = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   214→    cases = [CaseDefinition.from_dict(entry) for entry in payload["cases"]]
   215→    seen: set[str] = set()
   216→    for case in cases:
   217→        if case.case_id in seen:
   218→            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate case_id in manifest: {case.case_id}")
   219→        seen.add(case.case_id)
   220→    return cases

   223→def load_db_snapshots(snapshot_path: Path = DEFAULT_DB_SNAPSHOTS_PATH) -> dict[str, Any]:
   224→    global _DB_SNAPSHOTS_CACHE
   225→    if _DB_SNAPSHOTS_CACHE is None:
   226→        payload = json.loads(snapshot_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   227→        _DB_SNAPSHOTS_CACHE = payload["snapshots"]
   228→    return _DB_SNAPSHOTS_CACHE
   229→
   230→
   231→def filter_case_definitions(
   232→    cases: list[CaseDefinition],
   233→    *,
   234→    case_ids: set[str] | None = None,
   235→    task_types: set[str] | None = None,
   236→    tags: set[str] | None = None,
   237→    families: set[str] | None = None,
   238→    include_non_default: bool = False,
   239→) -> list[CaseDefinition]:
   240→    selected: list[CaseDefinition] = []
   241→    for case in cases:
   242→        if not include_non_default and not case.default_enabled:
   243→            continue
   244→        if case_ids and case.case_id not in case_ids:
   245→            continue
   246→        if task_types and case.task_type not in task_types:
   247→            continue
   248→        if families and case.family not in families:
   249→            continue
   250→        if tags and not tags.intersection(case.tags):
   251→            continue
   252→        selected.append(case)
   253→    return selected
   254→
   255→
   256→def requirements_status(case: CaseDefinition) -> tuple[bool, list[str]]:
   257→    missing: list[str] = []
   258→    for requirement in case.requires:
   259→        checker = REQUIREMENT_CHECKERS.get(requirement)
   260→        if checker is None:
   261→            missing.append(f"unknown requirement:{requirement}")
   262→            continue
   263→        if not checker():
   264→            missing.append(requirement)
   265→    return (len(missing) == 0, missing)
   266→
   267→
   268→def format_summary_markdown(
   269→    results: list[CaseResult],
   270→    *,
   271→    started_at: str,
   272→    run_dir: Path,
   273→) -> str:
   274→    lines = [
   275→        "# Worker Matrix Summary",
   276→        "",
   277→        f"- Started: {started_at}",
   278→        f"- Run dir: `{run_dir}`",
   279→        f"- Total cases: {len(results)}",
   280→        "",
   281→        "| Case | Task Type | Status | Actual | Duration (s) | Output |",
   282→        "| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |",
   283→    ]
   284→    for result in results:
   285→        output = result.output_path or ""
   286→        lines.append(
   287→            f"| `{result.case_id}` | `{result.task_type}` | `{result.status}` | "
   288→            f"`{result.actual_outcome}` | {result.duration_seconds:.2f} | `{output}` |"
   289→        )
   290→    failed_ids = [result.case_id for result in results if result.status == "failed"]
   291→    if failed_ids:
   292→        lines.extend([
   293→            "",
   294→            "## Failed Cases",
   295→            "",
   296→            "```text",
   297→            "\n".join(failed_ids),
   298→            "```",
   299→        ])
   300→    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
   301→
   302→
   303→def parse_args(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> argparse.Namespace:
   304→    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Run manifest-driven worker smoke cases")
   305→    parser.add_argument("--manifest", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_MANIFEST_PATH)
   306→    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_OUTPUT_ROOT)
   307→    parser.add_argument("--case-id", action="append", default=[])
   308→    parser.add_argument("--task-type", action="append", default=[])
   309→    parser.add_argument("--tag", action="append", default=[])
   310→    parser.add_argument("--family", action="append", default=[])
   311→    parser.add_argument("--failed-from", type=Path, default=None)
   312→    parser.add_argument("--list-cases", action="store_true")
   313→    parser.add_argument("--all-cases", action="store_true")
   314→    parser.add_argument("--stop-on-failure", action="store_true")
   315→    return parser.parse_args(argv)
   316→
   317→
   318→def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
   319→    ensure_repo_on_path()
   320→    args = parse_args(argv)
   321→    cases = load_case_definitions(args.manifest)
   322→
   323→    failed_case_ids: set[str] = set()
   324→    if args.failed_from:
   325→        failed_payload = json.loads(args.failed_from.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   326→        failed_case_ids = {
   327→            item["case_id"]
   328→            for item in failed_payload.get("results", [])
   329→            if item.get("status") == "failed"
   330→        }
   331→
   332→    combined_case_ids = set(args.case_id) | failed_case_ids
   333→    selected = filter_case_definitions(
   334→        cases,
   335→        case_ids=combined_case_ids or None,
   336→        task_types=set(args.task_type) or None,
   337→        tags=set(args.tag) or None,
   338→        families=set(args.family) or None,
   339→        include_non_default=args.all_cases or bool(args.case_id) or bool(failed_case_ids),
   340→    )
   341→
   342→    if args.list_cases:
   343→        for case in selected:
   344→            tags = ",".join(case.tags)
   345→            print(f"{case.case_id:28} {case.task_type:20} {case.family:18} {tags}")
   346→        return 0
   347→
   348→    if not selected:
   349→        print("No worker matrix cases selected.", file=sys.stderr)
   350→        return 1
   351→
   352→    started_at = _utc_timestamp()
   353→    run_dir = args.output_dir / started_at
   354→    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   355→
   356→    manifest_snapshot = [asdict(case) for case in selected]
   357→    _write_json(run_dir / "selected_cases.json", manifest_snapshot)
   358→
   359→    print(f"Running {len(selected)} worker matrix case(s) into {run_dir}")
   360→
   361→    results: list[CaseResult] = []
   362→    for case in selected:
   363→        result = run_case(case, run_dir)
   364→        results.append(result)
   365→        print(f"[{result.status.upper():7}] {case.case_id} -> {result.actual_outcome}")
   366→        if args.stop_on_failure and result.status == "failed":
   367→            break
   368→
   369→    summary_payload = {
   370→        "started_at": started_at,
   371→        "run_dir": str(run_dir),
   372→        "results": [asdict(result) for result in results],
   373→    }
   374→    _write_json(run_dir / "summary.json", summary_payload)
   375→    (run_dir / "summary.md").write_text(
   376→        format_summary_markdown(results, started_at=started_at, run_dir=run_dir),
   377→        encoding="utf-8",
   378→    )
   379→
   380→    failed_ids = [result.case_id for result in results if result.status == "failed"]
   381→    (run_dir / "failures.txt").write_text("\n".join(failed_ids) + ("\n" if failed_ids else ""), encoding="utf-8")
   382→    rerun_lines = [
   383→        "#!/usr/bin/env bash",
   384→        "set -euo pipefail",
   385→        f"cd {shlex.quote(str(REPO_ROOT))}",
   386→        "python scripts/run_worker_matrix.py \\",
   387→    ]
   388→    if failed_ids:
   389→        for case_id in failed_ids[:-1]:
   390→            rerun_lines.append(f"  --case-id {shlex.quote(case_id)} \\")
   391→        rerun_lines.append(f"  --case-id {shlex.quote(failed_ids[-1])}")
   392→    else:
   393→        rerun_lines.append("  --list-cases")
   394→    rerun_path = run_dir / "rerun_failed.sh"
   395→    rerun_path.write_text("\n".join(rerun_lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
   396→    rerun_path.chmod(0o755)
   397→
   398→    return 1 if failed_ids else 0
   399→
   400→
   401→def run_case(case: CaseDefinition, run_dir: Path) -> CaseResult:
   402→    ensure_repo_on_path()
   403→    case_dir = run_dir / case.case_id
   404→    case_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   405→    log_path = case_dir / "worker.log"
   406→    _write_json(case_dir / "case_definition.json", asdict(case))
   407→
   408→    requirements_ok, missing_requirements = requirements_status(case)
   409→    if not requirements_ok:
   410→        result = CaseResult(
   411→            case_id=case.case_id,
   412→            task_type=case.task_type,
   413→            family=case.family,
   414→            status="skipped",
   415→            expected_outcome=case.expected_outcome,
   416→            actual_outcome="skipped",
   417→            duration_seconds=0.0,
   418→            error_message=f"Missing requirements: {', '.join(missing_requirements)}",
   419→            log_path=str(log_path),
   420→            case_dir=str(case_dir),
   421→        )
   422→        _write_json(case_dir / "result.json", asdict(result))
   423→        return result
   424→
   425→    try:
   426→        prepared = CASE_BUILDERS[case.builder](case, case_dir)
   427→    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
   428→        tb_path = case_dir / "traceback.txt"
   429→        tb_path.write_text(traceback.format_exc(), encoding="utf-8")
   430→        result = CaseResult(
   431→            case_id=case.case_id,
   432→            task_type=case.task_type,
   433→            family=case.family,
   434→            status="failed",
   435→            expected_outcome=case.expected_outcome,
   436→            actual_outcome="failure",
   437→            duration_seconds=0.0,
   438→            error_message=f"Builder {case.builder!r} crashed: {exc}",
   439→            log_path=str(log_path),
   440→            case_dir=str(case_dir),
   441→            traceback_path=str(tb_path),
   442→        )
   443→        _write_json(case_dir / "result.json", asdict(result))
   444→        return result
   445→
   446→    _write_json(case_dir / "prepared_input.json", {
   447→        "task_type": prepared.definition.task_type,
   448→        "project_id": prepared.project_id,
   449→        "params": _json_safe(prepared.params),
   450→        "notes": _json_safe(prepared.notes),
   451→    })
   452→
   453→    started = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
   454→    actual_outcome = "failure"
   455→    output_path: str | None = None
   456→    error_message: str | None = None
   457→    traceback_path: str | None = None
   458→
   459→    with log_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as log_file:
   460→        tee_stdout = TeeWriter(sys.__stdout__, log_file)
   461→        tee_stderr = TeeWriter(sys.__stderr__, log_file)
   462→        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(tee_stdout), contextlib.redirect_stderr(tee_stderr):
   463→            started_marker = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
   464→            print(
   465→                f"[WORKER_MATRIX][CASE_START] case_id={case.case_id} "
   466→                f"task_type={case.task_type} started_at={started_marker}"
   467→            )
   468→            try:
   469→                with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
   470→                    for patcher in prepared.patchers:
   471→                        stack.enter_context(patcher)
   472→
   473→                    worker_mod = __import__("worker")
   474→                    from source.core.log import enable_debug_mode
   475→
   476→                    enable_debug_mode()
   477→                    raw_result = worker_mod.process_single_task(
   478→                        task_params_dict=copy.deepcopy(prepared.params),
   479→                        main_output_dir_base=prepared.main_output_dir,
   480→                        task_type=prepared.definition.task_type,
   481→                        project_id_for_task=prepared.project_id,
   482→                        task_queue=prepared.task_queue,
   483→                        colour_match_videos=prepared.colour_match_videos,
   484→                        mask_active_frames=prepared.mask_active_frames,
   485→                    )
   486→                success, output_path, error_message = _normalize_worker_result(raw_result)
   487→                actual_outcome = "success" if success else "failure"
   488→                print(
   489→                    f"[WORKER_MATRIX][CASE_END] case_id={case.case_id} "
   490→                    f"outcome={actual_outcome} output_path={output_path or ''} "
   491→                    f"error={error_message or ''}"
   492→                )
   493→            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
   494→                error_message = str(exc)
   495→                actual_outcome = "failure"
   496→                traceback_path = str(case_dir / "traceback.txt")
   497→                (case_dir / "traceback.txt").write_text(traceback.format_exc(), encoding="utf-8")
   498→                print(
   499→                    f"[WORKER_MATRIX][CASE_EXCEPTION] case_id={case.case_id} "
   500→                    f"error={error_message}"
   501→                )
   502→
   503→    duration_seconds = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - started).total_seconds()
   504→    expectation_matched = actual_outcome == case.expected_outcome
   505→    status = "passed" if expectation_matched else "failed"
   506→
   507→    result = CaseResult(
   508→        case_id=case.case_id,
   509→        task_type=case.task_type,
   510→        family=case.family,
   511→        status=status,
   512→        expected_outcome=case.expected_outcome,
   513→        actual_outcome=actual_outcome,
   514→        duration_seconds=duration_seconds,
   515→        output_path=output_path,
   516→        error_message=error_message,
   517→        log_path=str(log_path),
   518→        case_dir=str(case_dir),
   519→        traceback_path=traceback_path,
   520→        notes=_json_safe(prepared.notes),
   521→    )
   522→    _write_json(case_dir / "result.json", asdict(result))
   523→    return result
   524→
   525→
   526→def _normalize_worker_result(raw_result: Any) -> tuple[bool, str | None, str | None]:
   527→    if hasattr(raw_result, "outcome"):
   528→        from source.core.params.task_result import TaskOutcome
   529→
   530→        outcome = raw_result.outcome
   531→        if outcome == TaskOutcome.FAILED:
   532→            return False, None, getattr(raw_result, "error_message", None) or getattr(raw_result, "output_path", None)
   533→        if outcome in (TaskOutcome.ORCHESTRATING, TaskOutcome.ORCHESTRATOR_COMPLETE):
   534→            return False, None, f"Unexpected orchestrator outcome: {outcome.value}"
   535→        return True, getattr(raw_result, "output_path", None), None
   536→
   537→    if isinstance(raw_result, tuple) and len(raw_result) == 2:
   538→        success, value = raw_result
   539→        return bool(success), value if success else None, None if success else value
   540→
   541→    raise TypeError(f"Unsupported worker result shape: {type(raw_result).__name__}")
   542→

   544→def _build_direct_queue_case(
   545→    case: CaseDefinition,
   546→    case_dir: Path,
   547→    *,
   548→    params: dict[str, Any],
   549→    expected_model: str | None = None,
   550→    expected_parameters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   551→    patchers: list[Any] | None = None,
   552→    notes: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   553→    ) -> PreparedCase:
   554→    output_dir = case_dir / "outputs"
   555→    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   556→    case_params = copy.deepcopy(params)
   557→    case_params.setdefault("task_id", f"{case.case_id}-task")
   558→    queue = FakeImmediateTaskQueue(
   559→        output_dir=output_dir,
   560→        task_type=case.task_type,
   561→        case_dir=case_dir,
   562→        expected_model=expected_model,
   563→        expected_parameters=expected_parameters,
   564→    )
   565→    return PreparedCase(
   566→        definition=case,
   567→        params=case_params,
   568→        project_id=None,
   569→        main_output_dir=output_dir,
   570→        task_queue=queue,
   571→        patchers=patchers or [],
   572→        notes=notes or {},
   573→    )

   744→def _create_test_image(path: Path, text: str) -> Path:
   745→    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   746→    image = Image.new("RGB", (256, 256), color=(24, 64, 96))
   747→    pixels = image.load()
   748→    for x in range(32, 224):
   749→        for y in range(96, 160):
   750→            pixels[x, y] = (180, 80, 32)
   751→    image.save(path)
   752→    return path
   753→

   755→def _create_test_video(path: Path, *, width: int = 320, height: int = 180, frames: int = 6, fps: int = 16) -> Path:
   756→    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   757→    fourcc = cv2.VideoWriter_fourcc(*"mp4v")
   758→    writer = cv2.VideoWriter(str(path), fourcc, fps, (width, height))
   759→    for frame_idx in range(frames):
   760→        image = np.zeros((height, width, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
   761→        image[:, :, 0] = (frame_idx * 25) % 255
   762→        image[:, :, 1] = 80
   763→        image[:, :, 2] = 200 - (frame_idx * 10)
   764→        writer.write(image)
   765→    writer.release()
   766→    return path

   823→    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):

    67→def move_wgp_output_to_task_type_dir(output_path: str, task_type: str, task_id: str, main_output_dir_base: Path) -> str:
    68→    """
    69→    Move WGP-generated output from base directory to task-type subdirectory.
    70→
    71→    This function handles post-processing of WGP outputs to organize them by task_type.
    72→    WGP generates all files to a globally-configured base directory, so we move them
    73→    to task-type subdirectories after generation completes.
    74→
    75→    Args:
    76→        output_path: Path to the WGP-generated file (in base directory)
    77→        task_type: Task type (e.g., "vace", "flux", "t2v")
    78→        task_id: Task ID
    79→        main_output_dir_base: Base output directory
    80→
    81→    Returns:
    82→        New path if file was moved, original path otherwise
    83→    """
    84→    # Only process WGP task types
    85→    from source.task_handlers.tasks.task_types import WGP_TASK_TYPES
    86→    if task_type not in WGP_TASK_TYPES:
    87→        return output_path
    88→
    89→    try:
    90→        output_file = Path(output_path)
    91→
    92→        # Check if file exists
    93→        if not output_file.exists():
    94→            headless_logger.debug(f"Output file doesn't exist, skipping move: {output_path}", task_id=task_id)
    95→            return output_path
    96→
    97→        # Check if file is in base directory (not already in a subdirectory)
    98→        # If the parent directory is main_output_dir_base, it's in base directory
    99→        if output_file.parent.resolve() != main_output_dir_base.resolve():
   100→            headless_logger.debug(f"Output already in subdirectory, skipping move: {output_path}", task_id=task_id)
   101→            return output_path
   102→
   103→        # Generate new path in task-type subdirectory
   104→        filename = output_file.name
   105→        new_path, _ = prepare_output_path(
   106→            task_id=task_id,
   107→            filename=filename,
   108→            main_output_dir_base=main_output_dir_base,
   109→            task_type=task_type
   110→        )
   111→
   112→        # Move the file
   113→        headless_logger.info(
   114→            f"Moving WGP output to task-type directory: {output_file} → {new_path} (task_type={task_type})",
   115→            task_id=task_id
   116→        )
   117→
   118→        # Ensure destination directory exists
   119→        new_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   120→
   121→        # Move the file
   122→        shutil.move(str(output_file), str(new_path))
   123→
   124→        headless_logger.success(f"Moved WGP output to {new_path}", task_id=task_id)
   125→        return str(new_path)
   126→
   127→    except (OSError, shutil.Error, ValueError) as e:
   128→        headless_logger.error(f"Failed to move WGP output to task-type directory: {e}", task_id=task_id, exc_info=True)
   129→        # Return original path if move fails
   130→        return output_path

   174→        if output_location_to_db:

   176→                output_path=output_location_to_db,

   188→    # Return structured TaskResult when the dispatch returned one, preserving

   190→    if isinstance(result, TaskResult):

1→"""Structured result type for task handlers.
     2→
     3→Replaces the (bool, str) return convention with a proper dataclass.
     4→Eliminates magic string prefix parsing ("[ORCHESTRATOR_COMPLETE]", etc.)
     5→by encoding the outcome as an enum.
     6→
     7→Usage:
     8→    from source.core.params.task_result import TaskResult, TaskOutcome
     9→
    10→    # Simple success
    11→    return TaskResult.success(output_path="/path/to/output.mp4")
    12→
    13→    # Orchestrator complete
    14→    return TaskResult.orchestrator_complete(output_path="/path/to/final.mp4", thumbnail_url="...")
    15→
    16→    # Still orchestrating (children in progress)
    17→    return TaskResult.orchestrating("3/5 segments complete")
    18→
    19→    # Failure
    20→    return TaskResult.failed("Model not found")
    21→"""
    22→
    23→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    24→from enum import Enum
    25→from typing import Optional
    26→
    27→
    28→class TaskOutcome(Enum):
    29→    SUCCESS = "success"
    30→    FAILED = "failed"
    31→    ORCHESTRATING = "orchestrating"
    32→    ORCHESTRATOR_COMPLETE = "orchestrator_complete"
    33→
    34→
    35→@dataclass(frozen=True)
    36→class TaskResult:
    37→    """Structured result from a task handler."""
    38→
    39→    outcome: TaskOutcome
    40→    output_path: Optional[str] = None
    41→    error_message: Optional[str] = None
    42→    thumbnail_url: Optional[str] = None
    43→    metadata: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    44→
    45→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    46→    # Convenience constructors
    47→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    48→
    49→    @classmethod
    50→    def success(cls, output_path: str, **metadata) -> "TaskResult":
    51→        return cls(outcome=TaskOutcome.SUCCESS, output_path=output_path, metadata=metadata)
    52→
    53→    @classmethod
    54→    def failed(cls, message: str) -> "TaskResult":
    55→        return cls(outcome=TaskOutcome.FAILED, error_message=message)
    56→
    57→    @classmethod
    58→    def orchestrator_complete(
    59→        cls, output_path: str, thumbnail_url: Optional[str] = None
    60→    ) -> "TaskResult":
    61→        return cls(
    62→            outcome=TaskOutcome.ORCHESTRATOR_COMPLETE,
    63→            output_path=output_path,
    64→            thumbnail_url=thumbnail_url,
    65→        )
    66→
    67→    @classmethod
    68→    def orchestrating(cls, message: str) -> "TaskResult":
    69→        return cls(outcome=TaskOutcome.ORCHESTRATING, output_path=message)
    70→
    71→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    72→    # Properties
    73→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    74→
    75→    @property
    76→    def is_success(self) -> bool:
    77→        """True for SUCCESS and ORCHESTRATOR_COMPLETE outcomes."""
    78→        return self.outcome in (TaskOutcome.SUCCESS, TaskOutcome.ORCHESTRATOR_COMPLETE)
    79→
    80→    @property
    81→    def is_terminal(self) -> bool:
    82→        """True for outcomes that indicate the task is done (success or failed)."""
    83→        return self.outcome in (
    84→            TaskOutcome.SUCCESS,
    85→            TaskOutcome.FAILED,
    86→            TaskOutcome.ORCHESTRATOR_COMPLETE,
    87→        )
    88→
    89→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    90→    # Backward compatibility: tuple unpacking
    91→    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    92→
    93→    def __iter__(self):
    94→        """Allow ``success, output = result`` for backward compat.
    95→
    96→        Maps to the old (bool, str|None) convention:
    97→        - SUCCESS → (True, output_path)
    98→        - ORCHESTRATOR_COMPLETE → (True, output_path)
    99→        - ORCHESTRATING → (True, output_path)  # message in output_path
   100→        - FAILED → (False, error_message)
   101→        """
   102→        if self.outcome == TaskOutcome.FAILED:
   103→            yield False
   104→            yield self.error_message
   105→        else:
   106→            yield True
   107→            yield self.output_path
   108→

   101→_MISSING = object()

   103→def _get_param(key, *sources, default=_MISSING, prefer_truthy: bool = False):
   104→    """
   105→    Get a parameter from multiple sources with precedence (first source wins).
   106→
   107→    By default, only skips None values.
   108→    If prefer_truthy=True, also skips falsy non-bool values (e.g. "", {}, [], 0),
   109→    matching historical `a or b` fallback semantics while still preserving explicit booleans.
   110→    """
   111→    for source in sources:
   112→        if not source or key not in source:
   113→            continue
   114→
   115→        value = source[key]
   116→        if value is None:
   117→            continue
   118→
   119→        if prefer_truthy and not isinstance(value, bool) and not value:
   120→            continue
   121→
   122→        return value
   123→
   124→    return None if default is _MISSING else default
   125→
   126→def _resolve_segment_context(task_params_dict: dict, is_standalone: bool, task_id: str) -> SegmentContext:
   127→    """Resolve mode, orchestrator_details, individual_params, and segment identity.
   128→
   129→    Handles orchestrator vs standalone mode, fetching orchestrator_details from the DB
   130→    if not provided inline.
   131→
   132→    Raises ValueError if required fields are missing.
   133→    """
   134→    segment_params = task_params_dict
   135→    orchestrator_task_id_ref = segment_params.get("orchestrator_task_id_ref")
   136→    orchestrator_run_id = segment_params.get("orchestrator_run_id")
   137→    segment_idx = segment_params.get("segment_index")
   138→
   139→    # Get orchestrator_details (canonical name) or full_orchestrator_payload (legacy alias)
   140→    orchestrator_details: dict = segment_params.get("orchestrator_details") or segment_params.get("full_orchestrator_payload")
   141→
   142→    if is_standalone:
   143→        # Standalone mode: use provided payload, default segment_idx to 0
   144→        if segment_idx is None:
   145→            segment_idx = 0
   146→        if not orchestrator_details:
   147→            raise ValueError(f"Individual travel segment {task_id} missing orchestrator_details")
   148→        headless_logger.debug(f"Running in standalone mode (individual_travel_segment)", task_id=task_id)
   149→    else:
   150→        # Orchestrator mode: require segment_index and either inline orchestrator_details or ability to fetch
   151→        if segment_idx is None:
   152→            raise ValueError(f"Travel segment {task_id} missing segment_index")
   153→
   154→        # If orchestrator_details not inline, try to fetch from parent task
   155→        if not orchestrator_details:
   156→            if not orchestrator_task_id_ref:
   157→                raise ValueError(f"Travel segment {task_id} missing orchestrator_details and orchestrator_task_id_ref")
   158→            orchestrator_task_raw_params_json = db_ops.get_task_params(orchestrator_task_id_ref)
   159→            if orchestrator_task_raw_params_json:
   160→                fetched_params = json.loads(orchestrator_task_raw_params_json) if isinstance(orchestrator_task_raw_params_json, str) else orchestrator_task_raw_params_json
   161→                orchestrator_details = fetched_params.get("orchestrator_details")
   162→
   163→        if not orchestrator_details:
   164→            raise ValueError(f"Travel segment {task_id}: Could not retrieve orchestrator_details")
   165→
   166→    # individual_segment_params has highest priority for segment-specific overrides
   167→    individual_params: IndividualSegmentParams = segment_params.get("individual_segment_params", {})
   168→
   169→    return SegmentContext(
   170→        mode="standalone" if is_standalone else "orchestrator",
   171→        orchestrator_details=orchestrator_details,
   172→        individual_params=individual_params,
   173→        segment_idx=segment_idx,

   175→        orchestrator_task_id_ref=orchestrator_task_id_ref,
   176→        orchestrator_run_id=orchestrator_run_id,
   177→    )

   174→        output_path: str | None = None
   175→        if not validation_errors and not self.fail_message:
   176→            output_path = str(_create_synthetic_output(
   177→                output_dir=self.output_dir,
   178→                task_id=generation_task.id,
   179→                task_type=self.task_type,
   180→            ))
   181→
   182→        if validation_errors:
   183→            message = "; ".join(validation_errors)
   184→            status = SimpleNamespace(
   185→                status="failed",
   186→                result_path=None,
   187→                error_message=message,
   188→                processing_time=0.0,
   189→            )
   190→        elif self.fail_message:
   191→            status = SimpleNamespace(
   192→                status="failed",
   193→                result_path=None,
   194→                error_message=self.fail_message,
   195→                processing_time=0.0,
   196→            )
   197→        else:
   198→            status = SimpleNamespace(
   199→                status="completed",
   200→                result_path=output_path,
   201→                error_message=None,
   202→                processing_time=0.0,
   203→            )
   204→
   205→        self.status_map[generation_task.id] = status
   206→        return generation_task.id
   207→
   208→    def get_task_status(self, task_id: str) -> Any:
   209→        return self.status_map.get(task_id)
   210→
   211→
   212→def load_case_definitions(manifest_path: Path = DEFAULT_MANIFEST_PATH) -> list[CaseDefinition]:
   213→    payload = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   214→    cases = [CaseDefinition.from_dict(entry) for entry in payload["cases"]]
   215→    seen: set[str] = set()
   216→    for case in cases:
   217→        if case.case_id in seen:
   218→            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate case_id in manifest: {case.case_id}")
   219→        seen.add(case.case_id)
   220→    return cases
   221→
   222→
   223→def load_db_snapshots(snapshot_path: Path = DEFAULT_DB_SNAPSHOTS_PATH) -> dict[str, Any]:
   224→    global _DB_SNAPSHOTS_CACHE
   225→    if _DB_SNAPSHOTS_CACHE is None:
   226→        payload = json.loads(snapshot_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   227→        _DB_SNAPSHOTS_CACHE = payload["snapshots"]
   228→    return _DB_SNAPSHOTS_CACHE
   229→
   230→
   231→def filter_case_definitions(
   232→    cases: list[CaseDefinition],
   233→    *,
   234→    case_ids: set[str] | None = None,
   235→    task_types: set[str] | None = None,
   236→    tags: set[str] | None = None,
   237→    families: set[str] | None = None,
   238→    include_non_default: bool = False,
   239→) -> list[CaseDefinition]:
   240→    selected: list[CaseDefinition] = []
   241→    for case in cases:
   242→        if not include_non_default and not case.default_enabled:
   243→            continue
   244→        if case_ids and case.case_id not in case_ids:
   245→            continue
   246→        if task_types and case.task_type not in task_types:
   247→            continue
   248→        if families and case.family not in families:
   249→            continue
   250→        if tags and not tags.intersection(case.tags):
   251→            continue
   252→        selected.append(case)
   253→    return selected
   254→
   255→
   256→def requirements_status(case: CaseDefinition) -> tuple[bool, list[str]]:
   257→    missing: list[str] = []
   258→    for requirement in case.requires:
   259→        checker = REQUIREMENT_CHECKERS.get(requirement)
   260→        if checker is None:
   261→            missing.append(f"unknown requirement:{requirement}")
   262→            continue
   263→        if not checker():
   264→            missing.append(requirement)
   265→    return (len(missing) == 0, missing)
   266→
   267→
   268→def format_summary_markdown(
   269→    results: list[CaseResult],
   270→    *,
   271→    started_at: str,
   272→    run_dir: Path,
   273→) -> str:
   274→    lines = [
   275→        "# Worker Matrix Summary",
   276→        "",
   277→        f"- Started: {started_at}",
   278→        f"- Run dir: `{run_dir}`",
   279→        f"- Total cases: {len(results)}",
   280→        "",
   281→        "| Case | Task Type | Status | Actual | Duration (s) | Output |",
   282→        "| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |",
   283→    ]
   284→    for result in results:
   285→        output = result.output_path or ""
   286→        lines.append(
   287→            f"| `{result.case_id}` | `{result.task_type}` | `{result.status}` | "
   288→            f"`{result.actual_outcome}` | {result.duration_seconds:.2f} | `{output}` |"
   289→        )
   290→    failed_ids = [result.case_id for result in results if result.status == "failed"]
   291→    if failed_ids:
   292→        lines.extend([
   293→            "",
   294→            "## Failed Cases",
   295→            "",
   296→            "```text",
   297→            "\n".join(failed_ids),
   298→            "```",
   299→        ])
   300→    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
   301→
   302→
   303→def parse_args(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> argparse.Namespace:
   304→    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Run manifest-driven worker smoke cases")
   305→    parser.add_argument("--manifest", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_MANIFEST_PATH)
   306→    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_OUTPUT_ROOT)
   307→    parser.add_argument("--case-id", action="append", default=[])
   308→    parser.add_argument("--task-type", action="append", default=[])
   309→    parser.add_argument("--tag", action="append", default=[])
   310→    parser.add_argument("--family", action="append", default=[])
   311→    parser.add_argument("--failed-from", type=Path, default=None)
   312→    parser.add_argument("--list-cases", action="store_true")
   313→    parser.add_argument("--all-cases", action="store_true")
   314→    parser.add_argument("--stop-on-failure", action="store_true")
   315→    return parser.parse_args(argv)
   316→
   317→
   318→def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
   319→    ensure_repo_on_path()
   320→    args = parse_args(argv)
   321→    cases = load_case_definitions(args.manifest)
   322→
   323→    failed_case_ids: set[str] = set()
   324→    if args.failed_from:
   325→        failed_payload = json.loads(args.failed_from.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   326→        failed_case_ids = {
   327→            item["case_id"]
   328→            for item in failed_payload.get("results", [])
   329→            if item.get("status") == "failed"
   330→        }
   331→
   332→    combined_case_ids = set(args.case_id) | failed_case_ids
   333→    selected = filter_case_definitions(
   334→        cases,
   335→        case_ids=combined_case_ids or None,
   336→        task_types=set(args.task_type) or None,
   337→        tags=set(args.tag) or None,
   338→        families=set(args.family) or None,
   339→        include_non_default=args.all_cases or bool(args.case_id) or bool(failed_case_ids),
   340→    )
   341→
   342→    if args.list_cases:
   343→        for case in selected:
   344→            tags = ",".join(case.tags)
   345→            print(f"{case.case_id:28} {case.task_type:20} {case.family:18} {tags}")
   346→        return 0
   347→
   348→    if not selected:
   349→        print("No worker matrix cases selected.", file=sys.stderr)
   350→        return 1
   351→
   352→    started_at = _utc_timestamp()
   353→    run_dir = args.output_dir / started_at
   354→    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   355→
   356→    manifest_snapshot = [asdict(case) for case in selected]
   357→    _write_json(run_dir / "selected_cases.json", manifest_snapshot)
   358→
   359→    print(f"Running {len(selected)} worker matrix case(s) into {run_dir}")
   360→
   361→    results: list[CaseResult] = []
   362→    for case in selected:
   363→        result = run_case(case, run_dir)
   364→        results.append(result)
   365→        print(f"[{result.status.upper():7}] {case.case_id} -> {result.actual_outcome}")
   366→        if args.stop_on_failure and result.status == "failed":
   367→            break
   368→
   369→    summary_payload = {
   370→        "started_at": started_at,
   371→        "run_dir": str(run_dir),
   372→        "results": [asdict(result) for result in results],
   373→    }
   374→    _write_json(run_dir / "summary.json", summary_payload)
   375→    (run_dir / "summary.md").write_text(
   376→        format_summary_markdown(results, started_at=started_at, run_dir=run_dir),
   377→        encoding="utf-8",
   378→    )
   379→
   380→    failed_ids = [result.case_id for result in results if result.status == "failed"]
   381→    (run_dir / "failures.txt").write_text("\n".join(failed_ids) + ("\n" if failed_ids else ""), encoding="utf-8")
   382→    rerun_lines = [
   383→        "#!/usr/bin/env bash",
   384→        "set -euo pipefail",
   385→        f"cd {shlex.quote(str(REPO_ROOT))}",
   386→        "python scripts/run_worker_matrix.py \\",
   387→    ]
   388→    if failed_ids:
   389→        for case_id in failed_ids[:-1]:
   390→            rerun_lines.append(f"  --case-id {shlex.quote(case_id)} \\")
   391→        rerun_lines.append(f"  --case-id {shlex.quote(failed_ids[-1])}")
   392→    else:
   393→        rerun_lines.append("  --list-cases")
   394→    rerun_path = run_dir / "rerun_failed.sh"
   395→    rerun_path.write_text("\n".join(rerun_lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
   396→    rerun_path.chmod(0o755)
   397→
   398→    return 1 if failed_ids else 0
   399→
   400→
   401→def run_case(case: CaseDefinition, run_dir: Path) -> CaseResult:
   402→    ensure_repo_on_path()
   403→    case_dir = run_dir / case.case_id
   404→    case_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   405→    log_path = case_dir / "worker.log"
   406→    _write_json(case_dir / "case_definition.json", asdict(case))
   407→
   408→    requirements_ok, missing_requirements = requirements_status(case)
   409→    if not requirements_ok:
   410→        result = CaseResult(
   411→            case_id=case.case_id,
   412→            task_type=case.task_type,
   413→            family=case.family,
   414→            status="skipped",
   415→            expected_outcome=case.expected_outcome,
   416→            actual_outcome="skipped",
   417→            duration_seconds=0.0,
   418→            error_message=f"Missing requirements: {', '.join(missing_requirements)}",
   419→            log_path=str(log_path),
   420→            case_dir=str(case_dir),
   421→        )
   422→        _write_json(case_dir / "result.json", asdict(result))
   423→        return result
   424→
   425→    try:
   426→        prepared = CASE_BUILDERS[case.builder](case, case_dir)
   427→    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
   428→        tb_path = case_dir / "traceback.txt"
   429→        tb_path.write_text(traceback.format_exc(), encoding="utf-8")
   430→        result = CaseResult(
   431→            case_id=case.case_id,
   432→            task_type=case.task_type,
   433→            family=case.family,
   434→            status="failed",
   435→            expected_outcome=case.expected_outcome,
   436→            actual_outcome="failure",
   437→            duration_seconds=0.0,
   438→            error_message=f"Builder {case.builder!r} crashed: {exc}",
   439→            log_path=str(log_path),
   440→            case_dir=str(case_dir),
   441→            traceback_path=str(tb_path),
   442→        )
   443→        _write_json(case_dir / "result.json", asdict(result))
   444→        return result
   445→
   446→    _write_json(case_dir / "prepared_input.json", {
   447→        "task_type": prepared.definition.task_type,
   448→        "project_id": prepared.project_id,
   449→        "params": _json_safe(prepared.params),
   450→        "notes": _json_safe(prepared.notes),
   451→    })
   452→
   453→    started = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
   454→    actual_outcome = "failure"
   455→    output_path: str | None = None
   456→    error_message: str | None = None
   457→    traceback_path: str | None = None
   458→
   459→    with log_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as log_file:
   460→        tee_stdout = TeeWriter(sys.__stdout__, log_file)
   461→        tee_stderr = TeeWriter(sys.__stderr__, log_file)
   462→        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(tee_stdout), contextlib.redirect_stderr(tee_stderr):
   463→            started_marker = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
   464→            print(
   465→                f"[WORKER_MATRIX][CASE_START] case_id={case.case_id} "
   466→                f"task_type={case.task_type} started_at={started_marker}"
   467→            )
   468→            try:
   469→                with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
   470→                    for patcher in prepared.patchers:
   471→                        stack.enter_context(patcher)
   472→
   473→                    worker_mod = __import__("worker")
   474→                    from source.core.log import enable_debug_mode
   475→
   476→                    enable_debug_mode()
   477→                    raw_result = worker_mod.process_single_task(
   478→                        task_params_dict=copy.deepcopy(prepared.params),
   479→                        main_output_dir_base=prepared.main_output_dir,
   480→                        task_type=prepared.definition.task_type,
   481→                        project_id_for_task=prepared.project_id,
   482→                        task_queue=prepared.task_queue,
   483→                        colour_match_videos=prepared.colour_match_videos,
   484→                        mask_active_frames=prepared.mask_active_frames,
   485→                    )
   486→                success, output_path, error_message = _normalize_worker_result(raw_result)
   487→                actual_outcome = "success" if success else "failure"
   488→                print(
   489→                    f"[WORKER_MATRIX][CASE_END] case_id={case.case_id} "
   490→                    f"outcome={actual_outcome} output_path={output_path or ''} "
   491→                    f"error={error_message or ''}"
   492→                )
   493→            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
   494→                error_message = str(exc)
   495→                actual_outcome = "failure"
   496→                traceback_path = str(case_dir / "traceback.txt")
   497→                (case_dir / "traceback.txt").write_text(traceback.format_exc(), encoding="utf-8")
   498→                print(
   499→                    f"[WORKER_MATRIX][CASE_EXCEPTION] case_id={case.case_id} "
   500→                    f"error={error_message}"
   501→                )
   502→
   503→    duration_seconds = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - started).total_seconds()
   504→    expectation_matched = actual_outcome == case.expected_outcome
   505→    status = "passed" if expectation_matched else "failed"
   506→
   507→    result = CaseResult(
   508→        case_id=case.case_id,
   509→        task_type=case.task_type,
   510→        family=case.family,
   511→        status=status,
   512→        expected_outcome=case.expected_outcome,
   513→        actual_outcome=actual_outcome,
   514→        duration_seconds=duration_seconds,
   515→        output_path=output_path,
   516→        error_message=error_message,
   517→        log_path=str(log_path),
   518→        case_dir=str(case_dir),
   519→        traceback_path=traceback_path,
   520→        notes=_json_safe(prepared.notes),
   521→    )
   522→    _write_json(case_dir / "result.json", asdict(result))
   523→    return result
   524→
   525→
   526→def _normalize_worker_result(raw_result: Any) -> tuple[bool, str | None, str | None]:
   527→    if hasattr(raw_result, "outcome"):
   528→        from source.core.params.task_result import TaskOutcome
   529→
   530→        outcome = raw_result.outcome
   531→        if outcome == TaskOutcome.FAILED:
   532→            return False, None, getattr(raw_result, "error_message", None) or getattr(raw_result, "output_path", None)
   533→        if outcome in (TaskOutcome.ORCHESTRATING, TaskOutcome.ORCHESTRATOR_COMPLETE):
   534→            return False, None, f"Unexpected orchestrator outcome: {outcome.value}"
   535→        return True, getattr(raw_result, "output_path", None), None
   536→
   537→    if isinstance(raw_result, tuple) and len(raw_result) == 2:
   538→        success, value = raw_result
   539→        return bool(success), value if success else None, None if success else value
   540→
   541→    raise TypeError(f"Unsupported worker result shape: {type(raw_result).__name__}")
   542→

   544→def _build_direct_queue_case(
   545→    case: CaseDefinition,
   546→    case_dir: Path,
   547→    *,
   548→    params: dict[str, Any],
   549→    expected_model: str | None = None,
   550→    expected_parameters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   551→    patchers: list[Any] | None = None,
   552→    notes: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   553→    ) -> PreparedCase:
   554→    output_dir = case_dir / "outputs"
   555→    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   556→    case_params = copy.deepcopy(params)
   557→    case_params.setdefault("task_id", f"{case.case_id}-task")
   558→    queue = FakeImmediateTaskQueue(
   559→        output_dir=output_dir,
   560→        task_type=case.task_type,
   561→        case_dir=case_dir,
   562→        expected_model=expected_model,
   563→        expected_parameters=expected_parameters,
   564→    )
   565→    return PreparedCase(
   566→        definition=case,
   567→        params=case_params,
   568→        project_id=None,
   569→        main_output_dir=output_dir,
   570→        task_queue=queue,
   571→        patchers=patchers or [],
   572→        notes=notes or {},
   573→    )

   703→def build_wan22_individual_segment_db_like(case: CaseDefinition, case_dir: Path) -> PreparedCase:
   704→    start_image = _create_test_image(case_dir / "fixtures" / "wan22_start.png", text="W1")
   705→    end_image = _create_test_image(case_dir / "fixtures" / "wan22_end.png", text="W2")
   706→    snapshot, params = _load_snapshot_params(
   707→        "individual_travel_segment_wan22_i2v",
   708→        fixture_paths={
   709→            "wan22_start_image": start_image,
   710→            "wan22_end_image": end_image,
   711→        },
   712→    )
   713→    output_dir = case_dir / "outputs"
   714→    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   715→    queue = FakeImmediateTaskQueue(
   716→        output_dir=output_dir,
   717→        task_type="travel_segment",
   718→        case_dir=case_dir,
   719→        expected_model="wan_2_2_i2v_lightning_baseline_2_2_2",
   720→        expected_parameters={"video_length": 50},
   721→    )
   722→    return PreparedCase(
   723→        definition=case,
   724→        params=params,
   725→        project_id=None,
   726→        main_output_dir=output_dir,
   727→        task_queue=queue,
   728→        notes=_snapshot_notes(snapshot),
   729→    )

   744→def _create_test_image(path: Path, text: str) -> Path:
   745→    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   746→    image = Image.new("RGB", (256, 256), color=(24, 64, 96))
   747→    pixels = image.load()
   748→    for x in range(32, 224):
   749→        for y in range(96, 160):
   750→            pixels[x, y] = (180, 80, 32)
   751→    image.save(path)
   752→    return path
   753→
   754→
   755→def _create_test_video(path: Path, *, width: int = 320, height: int = 180, frames: int = 6, fps: int = 16) -> Path:
   756→    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   757→    fourcc = cv2.VideoWriter_fourcc(*"mp4v")
   758→    writer = cv2.VideoWriter(str(path), fourcc, fps, (width, height))
   759→    for frame_idx in range(frames):
   760→        image = np.zeros((height, width, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
   761→        image[:, :, 0] = (frame_idx * 25) % 255
   762→        image[:, :, 1] = 80
   763→        image[:, :, 2] = 200 - (frame_idx * 10)
   764→        writer.write(image)
   765→    writer.release()
   766→    return path
   767→
   768→
   769→def _create_synthetic_output(output_dir: Path, task_id: str, task_type: str) -> Path:
   770→    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   771→    if task_type in IMAGE_OUTPUT_TASK_TYPES:
   772→        return _create_test_image(output_dir / f"{task_id}.png", text=task_type[:2].upper())
   773→    return _create_test_video(output_dir / f"{task_id}.mp4")
   774→
   775→
   776→def _fake_hf_hub_download(*, filename: str, local_dir: str, **_: Any) -> str:
   777→    target = Path(local_dir) / filename
   778→    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   779→    target.write_bytes(b"fake-lora")
   780→    return str(target)
   781→
   782→
   783→def _load_snapshot_params(
   784→    snapshot_name: str,
   785→    *,
   786→    fixture_paths: dict[str, Path] | None = None,
   787→    fixture_urls: dict[str, str] | None = None,
   788→) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]:
   789→    snapshot = copy.deepcopy(load_db_snapshots()[snapshot_name])
   790→    replacements: dict[str, str] = {}
   791→    for key, value in (fixture_paths or {}).items():
   792→        replacements[f"__FIXTURE_PATH__:{key}"] = str(value)
   793→    for key, value in (fixture_urls or {}).items():
   794→        replacements[f"__FIXTURE_URL__:{key}"] = value
   795→    params = _replace_snapshot_tokens(snapshot["params"], replacements)
   796→    return snapshot, params
   797→
   798→
   799→def _replace_snapshot_tokens(value: Any, replacements: dict[str, str]) -> Any:
   800→    if isinstance(value, str):
   801→        return replacements.get(value, value)
   802→    if isinstance(value, dict):
   803→        return {[REDACTED](item, replacements) for key, item in value.items()}
   804→    if isinstance(value, list):
   805→        return [_replace_snapshot_tokens(item, replacements) for item in value]
   806→    return value
   807→
   808→
   809→def _snapshot_notes(snapshot: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
   810→    return {
   811→        "snapshot_name": snapshot["snapshot_name"],
   812→        "source_task_id": snapshot["source_task_id"],
   813→        "source_created_at": snapshot["source_created_at"],
   814→        "db_task_type": snapshot["task_type"],
   815→    }
   816→
   817→
   818→def _json_safe(value: Any) -> Any:
   819→    if isinstance(value, Path):
   820→        return str(value)
   821→    if isinstance(value, dict):
   822→        return {str(k): _json_safe(v) for k, v in value.items()}
   823→    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
   824→        return [_json_safe(item) for item in value]
   825→    if isinstance(value, np.integer):
   826→        return int(value)
   827→    if isinstance(value, np.floating):
   828→        return float(value)
   829→    if isinstance(value, np.ndarray):
   830→        return value.tolist()
   831→    if isinstance(value, bytes):
   832→        return value.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
   833→    return value
   834→
   835→
   836→def _write_json(path: Path, payload: Any) -> None:
   837→    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   838→    path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True), encoding="utf-8")
   839→
   840→
   841→def _utc_timestamp() -> str:
   842→    return datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%fZ")
   843→
   844→
   845→def _module_available(module_name: str) -> bool:
   846→    return importlib.util.find_spec(module_name) is not None
   847→
   848→
   849→REQUIREMENT_CHECKERS: dict[str, Callable[[], bool]] = {
   850→    "ffmpeg": lambda: shutil.which("ffmpeg") is not None and shutil.which("ffprobe") is not None,
   851→    "moviepy": lambda: _module_available("moviepy.editor"),
   852→}

   854→
   855→def ensure_repo_on_path() -> None:
   856→    repo_root_str = str(REPO_ROOT)
   857→    if repo_root_str not in sys.path:
   858→        sys.path.insert(0, repo_root_str)

   862→    raise SystemExit(main())

   350→        if "transformer_types" not in wgp_mod.server_config: wgp_mod.server_config["transformer_types"] = []

   399→

   401→            if _log_interceptor_instance:

   405→            raw_result = process_single_task(

   421→            if task_succeeded:

   425→
   426→                if current_task_type in orchestrator_types:

   428→                        db_ops.update_task_status_supabase(

   430→                            result.output_path, result.thumbnail_url)
   431→                    elif result and result.outcome == TaskOutcome.ORCHESTRATING:
   432→                        db_ops.update_task_status(current_task_id, db_ops.STATUS_IN_PROGRESS, result.output_path)
   433→                    elif isinstance(output_location, str) and output_location.startswith("[ORCHESTRATOR_COMPLETE]"):

   445→                    else:

   454→            else:

   456→                error_message = (result.error_message if result else output_location) or "Unknown error"
   457→                is_retryable, error_category, max_attempts = is_retryable_error(error_message)
   458→                current_attempts = task_info.get("attempts", 0)
   459→

   465→                    )
   466→                    db_ops.requeue_task_for_retry(

   472→                else:

   478→                    db_ops.update_task_status_supabase(current_task_id, db_ops.STATUS_FAILED, output_location)

    92→class HeadlessTaskQueue(WgpInitMixin):
    93→    """
    94→    Main task queue manager that integrates with wgp.py's existing queue system.

   212→    def wait_for_completion(self, task_id: str, timeout: float = 300.0) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   213→        """
   214→        Wait for a task to complete and return the result.
   215→
   216→        Args:
   217→            task_id: ID of the task to wait for
   218→            timeout: Maximum time to wait in seconds
   219→
   220→        Returns:
   221→            Dictionary with 'success', 'output_path', and optional 'error' keys
   222→        """
   223→        start_time = time.time()
   224→
   225→        while (time.time() - start_time) < timeout:
   226→            task_status = self.get_task_status(task_id)
   227→
   228→            if task_status is None:
   229→                return {
   230→                    "success": False,
   231→                    "error": f"Task {task_id} not found in queue"
   232→                }
   233→
   234→            if task_status.status == "completed":
   235→                return {
   236→                    "success": True,
   237→                    "output_path": task_status.result_path
   238→                }
   239→            elif task_status.status == "failed":
   240→                return {
   241→                    "success": False,
   242→                    "error": task_status.error_message or "Task failed with unknown error"
   243→                }
   244→
   245→            # Task is still pending or processing, wait a bit
   246→            time.sleep(1.0)
   247→
   248→        # Timeout reached
   249→        return {
   250→            "success": False,
   251→            "error": f"Task {task_id} did not complete within {timeout} seconds"
   252→        }
   253→
