   263→        if not checker():
   264→            missing.append(requirement)
   265→    return (len(missing) == 0, missing)
   266→
   267→
   268→def format_summary_markdown(
   269→    results: list[CaseResult],
   270→    *,
   271→    started_at: str,
   272→    run_dir: Path,
   273→) -> str:
   274→    lines = [
   275→        "# Worker Matrix Summary",
   276→        "",
   277→        f"- Started: {started_at}",
   278→        f"- Run dir: `{run_dir}`",
   279→        f"- Total cases: {len(results)}",
   280→        "",
   281→        "| Case | Task Type | Status | Actual | Duration (s) | Output |",
   282→        "| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |",
   283→    ]
   284→    for result in results:
   285→        output = result.output_path or ""
   286→        lines.append(
   287→            f"| `{result.case_id}` | `{result.task_type}` | `{result.status}` | "
   288→            f"`{result.actual_outcome}` | {result.duration_seconds:.2f} | `{output}` |"
   289→        )
   290→    failed_ids = [result.case_id for result in results if result.status == "failed"]
   291→    if failed_ids:
   292→        lines.extend([
   293→            "",
   294→            "## Failed Cases",
   295→            "",
   296→            "```text",
   297→            "\n".join(failed_ids),
   298→            "```",
   299→        ])
   300→    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
   301→
   302→
   303→def parse_args(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> argparse.Namespace:
   304→    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Run manifest-driven worker smoke cases")
   305→    parser.add_argument("--manifest", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_MANIFEST_PATH)
   306→    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_OUTPUT_ROOT)
   307→    parser.add_argument("--case-id", action="append", default=[])
   308→    parser.add_argument("--task-type", action="append", default=[])
   309→    parser.add_argument("--tag", action="append", default=[])
   310→    parser.add_argument("--family", action="append", default=[])
   311→    parser.add_argument("--failed-from", type=Path, default=None)
   312→    parser.add_argument("--list-cases", action="store_true")
   313→    parser.add_argument("--all-cases", action="store_true")
   314→    parser.add_argument("--stop-on-failure", action="store_true")
   315→    return parser.parse_args(argv)
   316→
   317→
   318→def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
   319→    ensure_repo_on_path()
   320→    args = parse_args(argv)
   321→    cases = load_case_definitions(args.manifest)
   322→
   323→    failed_case_ids: set[str] = set()
   324→    if args.failed_from:
   325→        failed_payload = json.loads(args.failed_from.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   326→        failed_case_ids = {
   327→            item["case_id"]
   328→            for item in failed_payload.get("results", [])
   329→            if item.get("status") == "failed"
   330→        }
   331→
   332→    combined_case_ids = set(args.case_id) | failed_case_ids
   333→    selected = filter_case_definitions(
   334→        cases,
   335→        case_ids=combined_case_ids or None,
   336→        task_types=set(args.task_type) or None,
   337→        tags=set(args.tag) or None,
   338→        families=set(args.family) or None,
   339→        include_non_default=args.all_cases or bool(args.case_id) or bool(failed_case_ids),
   340→    )
   341→
   342→    if args.list_cases:
   343→        for case in selected:
   344→            tags = ",".join(case.tags)
   345→            print(f"{case.case_id:28} {case.task_type:20} {case.family:18} {tags}")
   346→        return 0
   347→
   348→    if not selected:
   349→        print("No worker matrix cases selected.", file=sys.stderr)
   350→        return 1
   351→
   352→    started_at = _utc_timestamp()
   353→    run_dir = args.output_dir / started_at
   354→    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   355→
   356→    manifest_snapshot = [asdict(case) for case in selected]
   357→    _write_json(run_dir / "selected_cases.json", manifest_snapshot)
   358→
   359→    print(f"Running {len(selected)} worker matrix case(s) into {run_dir}")
   360→
   361→    results: list[CaseResult] = []
   362→    for case in selected:
   363→        result = run_case(case, run_dir)
   364→        results.append(result)
   365→        print(f"[{result.status.upper():7}] {case.case_id} -> {result.actual_outcome}")
   366→        if args.stop_on_failure and result.status == "failed":
   367→            break
   368→
   369→    summary_payload = {
   370→        "started_at": started_at,
   371→        "run_dir": str(run_dir),
   372→        "results": [asdict(result) for result in results],
   373→    }
   374→    _write_json(run_dir / "summary.json", summary_payload)
   375→    (run_dir / "summary.md").write_text(
   376→        format_summary_markdown(results, started_at=started_at, run_dir=run_dir),
   377→        encoding="utf-8",
   378→    )
   379→
   380→    failed_ids = [result.case_id for result in results if result.status == "failed"]
   381→    (run_dir / "failures.txt").write_text("\n".join(failed_ids) + ("\n" if failed_ids else ""), encoding="utf-8")
   382→    rerun_lines = [
   383→        "#!/usr/bin/env bash",
   384→        "set -euo pipefail",
   385→        f"cd {shlex.quote(str(REPO_ROOT))}",
   386→        "python scripts/run_worker_matrix.py \\",
   387→    ]
   388→    if failed_ids:
   389→        for case_id in failed_ids[:-1]:
   390→            rerun_lines.append(f"  --case-id {shlex.quote(case_id)} \\")
   391→        rerun_lines.append(f"  --case-id {shlex.quote(failed_ids[-1])}")
   392→    else:
   393→        rerun_lines.append("  --list-cases")
   394→    rerun_path = run_dir / "rerun_failed.sh"
   395→    rerun_path.write_text("\n".join(rerun_lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
   396→    rerun_path.chmod(0o755)
   397→
   398→    return 1 if failed_ids else 0
   399→
   400→
   401→def run_case(case: CaseDefinition, run_dir: Path) -> CaseResult:
   402→    ensure_repo_on_path()
   403→    case_dir = run_dir / case.case_id
   404→    case_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   405→    log_path = case_dir / "worker.log"
   406→    _write_json(case_dir / "case_definition.json", asdict(case))
   407→
   408→    requirements_ok, missing_requirements = requirements_status(case)
   409→    if not requirements_ok:
   410→        result = CaseResult(
   411→            case_id=case.case_id,
   412→            task_type=case.task_type,
   413→            family=case.family,
   414→            status="skipped",
   415→            expected_outcome=case.expected_outcome,
   416→            actual_outcome="skipped",
   417→            duration_seconds=0.0,
   418→            error_message=f"Missing requirements: {', '.join(missing_requirements)}",
   419→            log_path=str(log_path),
   420→            case_dir=str(case_dir),
   421→        )
   422→        _write_json(case_dir / "result.json", asdict(result))
   423→        return result
   424→
   425→    try:
   426→        prepared = CASE_BUILDERS[case.builder](case, case_dir)
   427→    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
   428→        tb_path = case_dir / "traceback.txt"
   429→        tb_path.write_text(traceback.format_exc(), encoding="utf-8")
   430→        result = CaseResult(
   431→            case_id=case.case_id,
   432→            task_type=case.task_type,
   433→            family=case.family,
   434→            status="failed",
   435→            expected_outcome=case.expected_outcome,
   436→            actual_outcome="failure",
   437→            duration_seconds=0.0,
   438→            error_message=f"Builder {case.builder!r} crashed: {exc}",
   439→            log_path=str(log_path),
   440→            case_dir=str(case_dir),
   441→            traceback_path=str(tb_path),
   442→        )
   443→        _write_json(case_dir / "result.json", asdict(result))
   444→        return result
   445→
   446→    _write_json(case_dir / "prepared_input.json", {
   447→        "task_type": prepared.definition.task_type,
   448→        "project_id": prepared.project_id,
   449→        "params": _json_safe(prepared.params),
   450→        "notes": _json_safe(prepared.notes),
   451→    })
   452→
   453→    started = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
   454→    actual_outcome = "failure"
   455→    output_path: str | None = None
   456→    error_message: str | None = None
   457→    traceback_path: str | None = None
   458→
   459→    with log_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as log_file:
   460→        tee_stdout = TeeWriter(sys.__stdout__, log_file)
   461→        tee_stderr = TeeWriter(sys.__stderr__, log_file)
   462→        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(tee_stdout), contextlib.redirect_stderr(tee_stderr):
   463→            started_marker = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
   464→            print(
   465→                f"[WORKER_MATRIX][CASE_START] case_id={case.case_id} "
   466→                f"task_type={case.task_type} started_at={started_marker}"
   467→            )
   468→            try:
   469→                with contextlib.ExitStack() as stack:
   470→                    for patcher in prepared.patchers:
   471→                        stack.enter_context(patcher)
   472→
   473→                    worker_mod = __import__("worker")
   474→                    from source.core.log import enable_debug_mode
   475→
   476→                    enable_debug_mode()
   477→                    raw_result = worker_mod.process_single_task(
   478→                        task_params_dict=copy.deepcopy(prepared.params),
   479→                        main_output_dir_base=prepared.main_output_dir,
   480→                        task_type=prepared.definition.task_type,
   481→                        project_id_for_task=prepared.project_id,
   482→                        task_queue=prepared.task_queue,
   483→                        colour_match_videos=prepared.colour_match_videos,
   484→                        mask_active_frames=prepared.mask_active_frames,
   485→                    )
   486→                success, output_path, error_message = _normalize_worker_result(raw_result)
   487→                actual_outcome = "success" if success else "failure"
   488→                print(
   489→                    f"[WORKER_MATRIX][CASE_END] case_id={case.case_id} "
   490→                    f"outcome={actual_outcome} output_path={output_path or ''} "
   491→                    f"error={error_message or ''}"
   492→                )
   493→            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
   494→                error_message = str(exc)
   495→                actual_outcome = "failure"
   496→                traceback_path = str(case_dir / "traceback.txt")
   497→                (case_dir / "traceback.txt").write_text(traceback.format_exc(), encoding="utf-8")
   498→                print(
   499→                    f"[WORKER_MATRIX][CASE_EXCEPTION] case_id={case.case_id} "
   500→                    f"error={error_message}"
   501→                )
   502→
   503→    duration_seconds = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - started).total_seconds()
   504→    expectation_matched = actual_outcome == case.expected_outcome
   505→    status = "passed" if expectation_matched else "failed"
   506→
   507→    result = CaseResult(
   508→        case_id=case.case_id,
   509→        task_type=case.task_type,
   510→        family=case.family,
   511→        status=status,
   512→        expected_outcome=case.expected_outcome,
   513→        actual_outcome=actual_outcome,
   514→        duration_seconds=duration_seconds,
   515→        output_path=output_path,
   516→        error_message=error_message,
   517→        log_path=str(log_path),
   518→        case_dir=str(case_dir),
   519→        traceback_path=traceback_path,
   520→        notes=_json_safe(prepared.notes),
   521→    )
   522→    _write_json(case_dir / "result.json", asdict(result))
   523→    return result
   524→
   525→
   526→def _normalize_worker_result(raw_result: Any) -> tuple[bool, str | None, str | None]:
   527→    if hasattr(raw_result, "outcome"):
   528→        from source.core.params.task_result import TaskOutcome
   529→
   530→        outcome = raw_result.outcome
   531→        if outcome == TaskOutcome.FAILED:
   532→            return False, None, getattr(raw_result, "error_message", None) or getattr(raw_result, "output_path", None)
   533→        if outcome in (TaskOutcome.ORCHESTRATING, TaskOutcome.ORCHESTRATOR_COMPLETE):
   534→            return False, None, f"Unexpected orchestrator outcome: {outcome.value}"
   535→        return True, getattr(raw_result, "output_path", None), None
   536→
   537→    if isinstance(raw_result, tuple) and len(raw_result) == 2:
   538→        success, value = raw_result
   539→        return bool(success), value if success else None, None if success else value
   540→
   541→    raise TypeError(f"Unsupported worker result shape: {type(raw_result).__name__}")
   542→

   544→def _build_direct_queue_case(
   545→    case: CaseDefinition,
   546→    case_dir: Path,
   547→    *,
   548→    params: dict[str, Any],
   549→    expected_model: str | None = None,
   550→    expected_parameters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   551→    patchers: list[Any] | None = None,
   552→    notes: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   553→    ) -> PreparedCase:
   554→    output_dir = case_dir / "outputs"
   555→    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   556→    case_params = copy.deepcopy(params)
   557→    case_params.setdefault("task_id", f"{case.case_id}-task")
   558→    queue = FakeImmediateTaskQueue(
   559→        output_dir=output_dir,
   560→        task_type=case.task_type,
   561→        case_dir=case_dir,
   562→        expected_model=expected_model,
   563→        expected_parameters=expected_parameters,
   564→    )
   565→    return PreparedCase(
   566→        definition=case,
   567→        params=case_params,
   568→        project_id=None,
   569→        main_output_dir=output_dir,
   570→        task_queue=queue,
   571→        patchers=patchers or [],
   572→        notes=notes or {},
   573→    )

   744→def _create_test_image(path: Path, text: str) -> Path:
   745→    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   746→    image = Image.new("RGB", (256, 256), color=(24, 64, 96))
   747→    pixels = image.load()
   748→    for x in range(32, 224):
   749→        for y in range(96, 160):
   750→            pixels[x, y] = (180, 80, 32)
   751→    image.save(path)
   752→    return path
   753→
   754→
   755→def _create_test_video(path: Path, *, width: int = 320, height: int = 180, frames: int = 6, fps: int = 16) -> Path:
   756→    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   757→    fourcc = cv2.VideoWriter_fourcc(*"mp4v")
   758→    writer = cv2.VideoWriter(str(path), fourcc, fps, (width, height))
   759→    for frame_idx in range(frames):
   760→        image = np.zeros((height, width, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
   761→        image[:, :, 0] = (frame_idx * 25) % 255
   762→        image[:, :, 1] = 80
   763→        image[:, :, 2] = 200 - (frame_idx * 10)
   764→        writer.write(image)
   765→    writer.release()
   766→    return path
   767→

   769→def _create_synthetic_output(output_dir: Path, task_id: str, task_type: str) -> Path:
   770→    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   771→    if task_type in IMAGE_OUTPUT_TASK_TYPES:
   772→        return _create_test_image(output_dir / f"{task_id}.png", text=task_type[:2].upper())
   773→    return _create_test_video(output_dir / f"{task_id}.mp4")

   776→def _fake_hf_hub_download(*, filename: str, local_dir: str, **_: Any) -> str:
   777→    target = Path(local_dir) / filename
   778→    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   779→    target.write_bytes(b"fake-lora")
   780→    return str(target)

   782→
   783→def _load_snapshot_params(
   784→    snapshot_name: str,
   785→    *,
   786→    fixture_paths: dict[str, Path] | None = None,
   787→    fixture_urls: dict[str, str] | None = None,
   788→) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]:
   789→    snapshot = copy.deepcopy(load_db_snapshots()[snapshot_name])
   790→    replacements: dict[str, str] = {}
   791→    for key, value in (fixture_paths or {}).items():
   792→        replacements[f"__FIXTURE_PATH__:{key}"] = str(value)
   793→    for key, value in (fixture_urls or {}).items():
   794→        replacements[f"__FIXTURE_URL__:{key}"] = value
   795→    params = _replace_snapshot_tokens(snapshot["params"], replacements)
   796→    return snapshot, params
   797→
   798→
   799→def _replace_snapshot_tokens(value: Any, replacements: dict[str, str]) -> Any:
   800→    if isinstance(value, str):
   801→        return replacements.get(value, value)
   802→    if isinstance(value, dict):
   803→        return {[REDACTED](item, replacements) for key, item in value.items()}
   804→    if isinstance(value, list):
   805→        return [_replace_snapshot_tokens(item, replacements) for item in value]
   806→    return value
   807→
   808→
   809→def _snapshot_notes(snapshot: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
   810→    return {
   811→        "snapshot_name": snapshot["snapshot_name"],
   812→        "source_task_id": snapshot["source_task_id"],
   813→        "source_created_at": snapshot["source_created_at"],
   814→        "db_task_type": snapshot["task_type"],
   815→    }
   816→
   817→
   818→def _json_safe(value: Any) -> Any:
   819→    if isinstance(value, Path):
   820→        return str(value)
   821→    if isinstance(value, dict):
   822→        return {str(k): _json_safe(v) for k, v in value.items()}
   823→    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
   824→        return [_json_safe(item) for item in value]
   825→    if isinstance(value, np.integer):
   826→        return int(value)
   827→    if isinstance(value, np.floating):
   828→        return float(value)
   829→    if isinstance(value, np.ndarray):
   830→        return value.tolist()
   831→    if isinstance(value, bytes):
   832→        return value.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
   833→    return value

   837→    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   838→    path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True), encoding="utf-8")

   846→    return importlib.util.find_spec(module_name) is not None
   847→
   848→
   849→REQUIREMENT_CHECKERS: dict[str, Callable[[], bool]] = {

    22→def switch_model_impl(queue: "HeadlessTaskQueue", model_key: str, worker_name: str) -> bool:
    23→    """
    24→    Ensure the correct model is loaded using wgp.py's model management.
    25→
    26→    This leverages the orchestrator's model loading while tracking
    27→    the change in our queue system. The orchestrator checks WGP's ground truth
    28→    (wgp.transformer_type) to determine if a switch is actually needed.
    29→
    30→    Returns:
    31→        bool: True if a model switch actually occurred, False if already loaded
    32→    """
    33→    # Ensure orchestrator is initialized before switching models
    34→    queue._ensure_orchestrator()
    35→
    36→    queue.logger.debug(f"{worker_name} ensuring model {model_key} is loaded (current: {queue.current_model})")
    37→    switch_start = time.time()
    38→
    39→    try:
    40→        # Use orchestrator's model loading - it checks WGP's ground truth
    41→        # and returns whether a switch actually occurred
    42→        switched = queue.orchestrator.load_model(model_key)
    43→
    44→        if switched:
    45→            # Only do switch-specific actions if a switch actually occurred
    46→            queue.logger.info(f"{worker_name} switched model: {queue.current_model} → {model_key}")
    47→
    48→            queue.stats["model_switches"] += 1
    49→            switch_time = time.time() - switch_start
    50→            queue.logger.info(f"Model switch completed in {switch_time:.1f}s")
    51→
    52→        # Always sync our tracking with orchestrator's state
    53→        queue.current_model = model_key
    54→        return switched
    55→
    56→    except (RuntimeError, ValueError, OSError) as e:
    57→        queue.logger.error(f"Model switch failed: {e}")
    58→        raise

    94→        raise

    99→
   100→    # Log the parsed config

   128→        finally:
   129→            if _saved_cwd != queue.wan_dir:

   132→    # Validate before conversion

   134→    if errors:

   150→        queue.logger.debug(f"[TASK_CONVERSION] Task {task.id}: LoRAs: {wgp_params.get('activated_loras', [])}")

    92→class HeadlessTaskQueue(WgpInitMixin):
    93→    """
    94→    Main task queue manager that integrates with wgp.py's existing queue system.
    95→
    96→    This class leverages wgp.py's built-in task management and state persistence
    97→    while providing a clean API for headless operation.

    99→    Mixins:

   102→    
   103→    def __init__(self, wan_dir: str, max_workers: int = 1, debug_mode: bool = False, main_output_dir: Optional[str] = None):
   104→        """
   105→        Initialize the headless task queue.
   106→
   107→        Args:
   108→            wan_dir: Path to WanGP directory

   117→        self.running = False

   132→            dummy_matanyone = types.ModuleType('preprocessing.matanyone')
   133→            dummy_app = types.ModuleType('preprocessing.matanyone.app')
   134→            def _noop_handler():

   138→                return _Dummy()
   139→            dummy_app.get_vmc_event_handler = _noop_handler  # type: ignore

   143→        except (TypeError, AttributeError, ImportError) as e:

   145→        # Don't import wgp during initialization to avoid CUDA/argparse conflicts

   212→    def wait_for_completion(self, task_id: str, timeout: float = 300.0) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   213→        """
   214→        Wait for a task to complete and return the result.
   215→
   216→        Args:
   217→            task_id: ID of the task to wait for
   218→            timeout: Maximum time to wait in seconds
   219→
   220→        Returns:
   221→            Dictionary with 'success', 'output_path', and optional 'error' keys
   222→        """
   223→        start_time = time.time()
   224→
   225→        while (time.time() - start_time) < timeout:
   226→            task_status = self.get_task_status(task_id)
   227→
   228→            if task_status is None:
   229→                return {
   230→                    "success": False,
   231→                    "error": f"Task {task_id} not found in queue"
   232→                }
   233→
   234→            if task_status.status == "completed":
   235→                return {
   236→                    "success": True,
   237→                    "output_path": task_status.result_path
   238→                }
   239→            elif task_status.status == "failed":
   240→                return {
   241→                    "success": False,
   242→                    "error": task_status.error_message or "Task failed with unknown error"
   243→                }
   244→
   245→            # Task is still pending or processing, wait a bit
   246→            time.sleep(1.0)
   247→
   248→        # Timeout reached
   249→        return {

   341→    def _convert_single_frame_video_to_png(self, task: GenerationTask, video_path: str, worker_name: str) -> str:
   342→        """
   343→        Convert a single-frame video to PNG format for single image tasks.
   344→        
   345→        This restores the functionality that was in the original single_image.py handler
   346→        where single-frame videos were converted to PNG files.
   347→        """
   348→        try:
   349→            import cv2
   350→            
   351→            video_path_obj = Path(video_path)
   352→            if not video_path_obj.exists():
   353→                self.logger.error(f"Video file does not exist for PNG conversion: {video_path}")
   354→                return video_path  # Return original path if conversion fails
   355→            
   356→            # Create PNG output path with sanitized filename to prevent upload issues
   357→            original_filename = video_path_obj.stem
   358→            
   359→            # Sanitize the filename for storage compatibility
   360→            try:
   361→                from source.utils import sanitize_filename_for_storage
   362→
   363→                sanitized_filename = sanitize_filename_for_storage(original_filename)
   364→                if not sanitized_filename:
   365→                    sanitized_filename = "generated_image"
   366→
   367→            except ImportError:
   368→                # Fallback sanitization if import fails
   369→                import re
   370→                sanitized_filename = re.sub(r'[§®©™@·º½¾¿¡~\x00-\x1F\x7F-\x9F<>:"/\\|?*,]', '', original_filename)
   371→                sanitized_filename = re.sub(r'\s+', '_', sanitized_filename.strip())
   372→                if not sanitized_filename:
   373→                    sanitized_filename = "generated_image"
   374→            
   375→            # Create PNG path with sanitized filename
   376→            png_path = video_path_obj.parent / f"{sanitized_filename}.png"
   377→            
   378→            # Log sanitization if filename changed
   379→            if sanitized_filename != original_filename:
   380→                self.logger.info(f"[PNG_CONVERSION] Task {task.id}: Sanitized filename '{original_filename}' -> '{sanitized_filename}'")
   381→            
   382→            self.logger.info(f"[PNG_CONVERSION] Task {task.id}: Converting {video_path_obj.name} to {png_path.name}")
   383→            
   384→            # Extract the first frame using OpenCV
   385→            cap = cv2.VideoCapture(str(video_path_obj))
   386→            try:
   387→                if cap.isOpened():
   388→                    ret, frame = cap.read()
   389→                    if ret:
   390→                        # Save the frame as PNG
   391→                        success = cv2.imwrite(str(png_path), frame)
   392→                        if success and png_path.exists():
   393→                            self.logger.info(f"[PNG_CONVERSION] Task {task.id}: Successfully saved PNG to {png_path}")
   394→                            
   395→                            # Clean up the original video file
   396→                            try:
   397→                                video_path_obj.unlink()
   398→                                self.logger.info(f"[PNG_CONVERSION] Task {task.id}: Removed original video file")
   399→                            except OSError as e_cleanup:
   400→                                self.logger.warning(f"[PNG_CONVERSION] Task {task.id}: Could not remove original video: {e_cleanup}")
   401→                            
   402→                            return str(png_path)
   403→                        else:
   404→                            self.logger.error(f"[PNG_CONVERSION] Task {task.id}: Failed to save PNG to {png_path}")
   405→                    else:
   406→                        self.logger.error(f"[PNG_CONVERSION] Task {task.id}: Failed to read frame from video")
   407→                else:
   408→                    self.logger.error(f"[PNG_CONVERSION] Task {task.id}: Failed to open video file")
   409→            finally:
   410→                cap.release()
   411→                
   412→        except ImportError:
   413→            self.logger.warning(f"[PNG_CONVERSION] Task {task.id}: OpenCV not available, keeping video format")
   414→        except (OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as e:
   415→            self.logger.error(f"[PNG_CONVERSION] Task {task.id}: Error during conversion: {e}")
   416→        
   417→        # Return original video path if conversion failed
   418→        return video_path

   429→    def _apply_sampler_cfg_preset(self, model_key: str, sample_solver: str, wgp_params: Dict[str, Any]):
   430→        """Apply sampler-specific CFG and flow_shift settings from model configuration."""
   431→        try:
   432→            # Import WGP to get model definition
   433→            # Protect sys.argv in case wgp hasn't been imported yet
   434→            _saved_argv = sys.argv[:]
   435→            try:
   436→                sys.argv = ["headless_model_management.py"]
   437→                import wgp
   438→            finally:
   439→                sys.argv = _saved_argv
   440→
   441→            model_def = wgp.get_model_def(model_key)
   442→            
   443→            # Check if model has sampler-specific presets
   444→            sampler_presets = model_def.get("sampler_cfg_presets", {})
   445→            if sample_solver in sampler_presets:
   446→                preset = sampler_presets[sample_solver]
   447→                
   448→                # Apply preset settings, but allow task parameters to override
   449→                applied_params = {}
   450→                for param, value in preset.items():
   451→                    if param not in wgp_params:  # Only apply if not explicitly set in task
   452→                        wgp_params[param] = value
   453→                        applied_params[param] = value
   454→                        
   455→                self.logger.info(f"Applied sampler '{sample_solver}' CFG preset: {applied_params}")
   456→            else:
   457→                self.logger.debug(f"No CFG preset found for sampler '{sample_solver}' in model '{model_key}'")
   458→                
   459→        except (ValueError, KeyError, AttributeError, TypeError, ImportError) as e:
   460→            self.logger.warning(f"Failed to apply sampler CFG preset: {e}")

   474→    """Main entry point for the headless service."""

   476→    parser.add_argument("--wan-dir", required=True, help="Path to WanGP directory")
   477→    parser.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=1, help="Number of worker threads")

   484→
   485→    # Initialize queue

   488→    # Setup signal handlers
   489→    def signal_handler(signum, frame):
   490→        queue_logger.essential("Received shutdown signal, stopping...")
   491→        task_queue.stop()
   492→        sys.exit(0)
   493→
   494→    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, signal_handler)
   495→    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, signal_handler)
   496→
   497→    try:
   498→        # Start services
   499→        task_queue.start()
   500→
   501→        queue_logger.essential(f"Headless queue started")
   502→        queue_logger.essential(f"WanGP directory: {args.wan_dir}")
   503→        queue_logger.essential(f"Workers: {args.workers}")
   504→        queue_logger.essential("Press Ctrl+C to stop...")
   505→
   506→        # Example: Submit some test tasks

   510→            # Test T2V task

   518→            )
   519→            task_queue.submit_task(t2v_task)
   520→
   521→        # Keep running until shutdown
   522→        while task_queue.running:
   523→            time.sleep(1.0)
   524→
   525→            # Print periodic status
   526→            if args.debug:
   527→                status = task_queue.get_queue_status()
   528→                queue_logger.debug(f"Queue: {status.pending_tasks} pending, "
   529→                      f"{status.completed_tasks} completed, "
   530→                      f"{status.failed_tasks} failed")
   531→
   532→    except KeyboardInterrupt:
   533→        queue_logger.essential("Shutdown requested by user")
   534→    except Exception as e:
   535→        queue_logger.error(f"Fatal error: {e}")
   536→        raise
   537→    finally:

   103→def _get_param(key, *sources, default=_MISSING, prefer_truthy: bool = False):
   104→    """
   105→    Get a parameter from multiple sources with precedence (first source wins).
   106→
   107→    By default, only skips None values.
   108→    If prefer_truthy=True, also skips falsy non-bool values (e.g. "", {}, [], 0),
   109→    matching historical `a or b` fallback semantics while still preserving explicit booleans.
   110→    """
   111→    for source in sources:
   112→        if not source or key not in source:
   113→            continue
   114→
   115→        value = source[key]
   116→        if value is None:
   117→            continue
   118→
   119→        if prefer_truthy and not isinstance(value, bool) and not value:
   120→            continue
   121→
   122→        return value
   123→
   124→    return None if default is _MISSING else default

   126→def _resolve_segment_context(task_params_dict: dict, is_standalone: bool, task_id: str) -> SegmentContext:
   127→    """Resolve mode, orchestrator_details, individual_params, and segment identity.
   128→
   129→    Handles orchestrator vs standalone mode, fetching orchestrator_details from the DB
   130→    if not provided inline.
   131→
   132→    Raises ValueError if required fields are missing.

   135→    orchestrator_task_id_ref = segment_params.get("orchestrator_task_id_ref")
   136→    orchestrator_run_id = segment_params.get("orchestrator_run_id")
   137→    segment_idx = segment_params.get("segment_index")
   138→
   139→    # Get orchestrator_details (canonical name) or full_orchestrator_payload (legacy alias)
   140→    orchestrator_details: dict = segment_params.get("orchestrator_details") or segment_params.get("full_orchestrator_payload")
   141→
   142→    if is_standalone:
   143→        # Standalone mode: use provided payload, default segment_idx to 0
   144→        if segment_idx is None:
   145→            segment_idx = 0
   146→        if not orchestrator_details:
   147→            raise ValueError(f"Individual travel segment {task_id} missing orchestrator_details")
   148→        headless_logger.debug(f"Running in standalone mode (individual_travel_segment)", task_id=task_id)
   149→    else:
   150→        # Orchestrator mode: require segment_index and either inline orchestrator_details or ability to fetch
   151→        if segment_idx is None:

   153→
   154→        # If orchestrator_details not inline, try to fetch from parent task

   217→        raise ValueError(f"Travel segment {task_id}: Invalid resolution format {parsed_res_wh_str}")
   218→    from source.utils.resolution_utils import get_model_grid_size
   219→    model_name = segment_params.get("model_name") or orchestrator_details.get("model_name")
   220→    grid_size = get_model_grid_size(model_name)
   221→    parsed_res_wh = snap_resolution_to_model_grid(parsed_res_raw, grid_size)
   222→
   223→    # Frame count: individual_segment_params.num_frames > top-level num_frames > segment_frames_target > segment_frames_expanded[idx]
   224→    total_frames_for_segment = (
   225→        individual_params.get("num_frames") or
   226→        segment_params.get("num_frames") or
   227→        segment_params.get("segment_frames_target")

   229→    if not total_frames_for_segment:
   230→        segment_frames = orchestrator_details.get("segment_frames_expanded", [])

   232→            total_frames_for_segment = segment_frames[segment_idx]
   233→        else:

   236→                f"segment_frames_expanded has {len(segment_frames)} entries)"

   247→    if not base_dir_path.is_absolute():

   273→def _resolve_image_references(ctx: SegmentContext, gen: GenerationInputs, task_id: str, is_standalone: bool) -> ImageRefs:
   274→    """Resolve start/end image reference paths and SVI predecessor video.
   275→
   276→    Handles SVI chaining (downloading predecessor video, extracting last frames),
   277→    non-SVI image resolution from multiple sources, and downloading URLs to local paths.
   278→    """
   279→    segment_params = ctx.segment_params
   280→    orchestrator_details = ctx.orchestrator_details
   281→    individual_params = ctx.individual_params
   282→    segment_idx = ctx.segment_idx
   283→    segment_processing_dir = gen.segment_processing_dir
   284→    debug_enabled = gen.debug_enabled
   285→
   286→    start_ref_path = None
   287→    end_ref_path = None
   288→
   289→    # Image resolution priority:
   290→    # 1. individual_segment_params.start_image_url / end_image_url
   291→    # 2. individual_segment_params.input_image_paths_resolved (array)
   292→    # 3. top-level input_image_paths_resolved
   293→    # 4. orchestrator_details images (indexed by segment_idx)
   294→
   295→    individual_images = individual_params.get("input_image_paths_resolved", [])
   296→    top_level_images = segment_params.get("input_image_paths_resolved", [])
   297→    orchestrator_images = orchestrator_details.get("input_image_paths_resolved", [])
   298→
   299→    task_logger.debug(f"[IMG_RESOLVE] Task {task_id}: segment_idx={segment_idx}, individual_images={len(individual_images)}, top_level_images={len(top_level_images)}, orchestrator_images={len(orchestrator_images)}")

     3→WanGP Headless Task Queue Manager
     4→
     5→A persistent service that maintains model state and processes generation tasks
     6→via a queue system. This script keeps models loaded in memory and delegates
     7→actual generation to headless_wgp.py while managing the queue, persistence,
     8→and task scheduling.
     9→
    10→Key Features:
    11→- Persistent model state (models stay loaded until switched)
    12→- Task queue with priority support
    13→- Auto model switching and memory management
    14→- Status monitoring and progress tracking
    15→- Uses wgp.py's native queue and state management
    16→- Hot-swappable task processing
    17→
    18→Usage:
    19→    # Start the headless service
    20→    python headless_model_management.py --wan-dir /path/to/WanGP --port 8080
    21→    
    22→    # Submit tasks via API or queue files
    23→    curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate \
    24→         -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    25→         -d '{"model": "vace_14B", "prompt": "mystical forest", "video_guide": "input.mp4"}'
    26→"""
    27→
    28→import os
    29→import sys
    30→import time
    31→
    32→import threading
    33→import queue
    34→import argparse
    35→import signal
    36→import logging
    37→from pathlib import Path
    38→from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Any
    39→from dataclasses import dataclass
    40→from datetime import datetime
    41→from source.core.log import queue_logger
    42→from source.task_handlers.queue.download_ops import switch_model_impl, convert_to_wgp_task_impl
    43→from source.task_handlers.queue.task_processor import (
    44→    worker_loop,
    45→    process_task_impl,
    46→    execute_generation_impl,
    47→    cleanup_memory_after_task,
    48→)
    49→from source.task_handlers.queue.queue_lifecycle import start_queue, stop_queue, submit_task_impl
    50→from source.task_handlers.queue.wgp_init import WgpInitMixin
    51→

    53→# Add WanGP to path for imports
    54→def setup_wgp_path(wan_dir: str):
    55→    """Setup WanGP path and imports."""
    56→    wan_dir = os.path.abspath(wan_dir)
    57→    if wan_dir not in sys.path:
    58→        sys.path.insert(0, wan_dir)
    59→    return wan_dir
    60→
    61→# Task definitions
    62→@dataclass
    63→class GenerationTask:
    64→    """Represents a single generation task."""
    65→    id: str
    66→    model: str
    67→    prompt: str
    68→    parameters: Dict[str, Any]
    69→    priority: int = 0
    70→    created_at: str = None
    71→    status: str = "pending"  # pending, processing, completed, failed
    72→    result_path: Optional[str] = None
    73→    error_message: Optional[str] = None
    74→    processing_time: Optional[float] = None
    75→    
    76→    def __post_init__(self):
    77→        if self.created_at is None:
    78→            self.created_at = datetime.now().isoformat()
    79→
    80→@dataclass 
    81→class QueueStatus:
    82→    """Current queue status information."""
    83→    pending_tasks: int
    84→    processing_task: Optional[str]
    85→    completed_tasks: int
    86→    failed_tasks: int
    87→    current_model: Optional[str]
    88→    uptime: float
    89→    memory_usage: Dict[str, Any]
    90→
    91→
    92→class HeadlessTaskQueue(WgpInitMixin):
    93→    """
    94→    Main task queue manager that integrates with wgp.py's existing queue system.
    95→
    96→    This class leverages wgp.py's built-in task management and state persistence
    97→    while providing a clean API for headless operation.
    98→
    99→    Mixins:
   100→        WgpInitMixin: CUDA warmup and lazy WanOrchestrator initialization
   101→    """
   102→    
   103→    def __init__(self, wan_dir: str, max_workers: int = 1, debug_mode: bool = False, main_output_dir: Optional[str] = None):
   104→        """
   105→        Initialize the headless task queue.
   106→
   107→        Args:
   108→            wan_dir: Path to WanGP directory
   109→            max_workers: Number of concurrent generation workers (recommend 1 for GPU)
   110→            debug_mode: Enable verbose debug logging (should match worker's --debug flag)
   111→            main_output_dir: Optional path for output directory. If not provided, defaults to
   112→                           'outputs' directory next to wan_dir (preserves backwards compatibility)
   113→        """
   114→        self.wan_dir = setup_wgp_path(wan_dir)
   115→        self.max_workers = max_workers
   116→        self.main_output_dir = main_output_dir
   117→        self.running = False
   118→        self.start_time = time.time()
   119→        self.debug_mode = debug_mode  # Now controlled by caller
   120→        
   121→        # Import wgp after path setup (protect sys.argv to prevent argument conflicts)
   122→        _saved_argv = sys.argv[:]
   123→        sys.argv = ["headless_wgp.py"]
   124→        # Headless stubs to avoid optional UI deps (tkinter/matanyone) during import
   125→        try:
   126→            import types
   127→            # Stub tkinter if not available
   128→            if 'tkinter' not in sys.modules:
   129→                sys.modules['tkinter'] = types.ModuleType('tkinter')
   130→            # Stub preprocessing.matanyone.app with minimal interface
   131→            dummy_pkg = types.ModuleType('preprocessing')
   132→            dummy_matanyone = types.ModuleType('preprocessing.matanyone')
   133→            dummy_app = types.ModuleType('preprocessing.matanyone.app')
   134→            def _noop_handler():
   135→                class _Dummy:
   136→                    def __getattr__(self, _):
   137→                        return None
   138→                return _Dummy()
   139→            dummy_app.get_vmc_event_handler = _noop_handler  # type: ignore
   140→            sys.modules['preprocessing'] = dummy_pkg
   141→            sys.modules['preprocessing.matanyone'] = dummy_matanyone
   142→            sys.modules['preprocessing.matanyone.app'] = dummy_app
   143→        except (TypeError, AttributeError, ImportError) as e:
   144→            logging.getLogger('HeadlessQueue').debug(f"Failed to set up headless UI stubs: {e}")
   145→        # Don't import wgp during initialization to avoid CUDA/argparse conflicts
   146→        # wgp will be imported lazily when needed (e.g., in _apply_sampler_cfg_preset)
   147→        # This allows the queue to initialize even if CUDA isn't ready yet
   148→        self.wgp = None
   149→        
   150→        # Restore sys.argv immediately (no wgp import, so no need for protection)
   151→        try:
   152→            sys.argv = _saved_argv
   153→        except (TypeError, AttributeError) as e:
   154→            logging.getLogger('HeadlessQueue').debug(f"Failed to restore sys.argv after init: {e}")
   155→        
   156→        # Defer orchestrator initialization to avoid CUDA init during queue setup
   157→        # Orchestrator imports wgp, which triggers deep imports that call torch.cuda
   158→        # We'll initialize it lazily when first needed
   159→        self.orchestrator = None
   160→        self._orchestrator_init_attempted = False
   161→        logging.getLogger('HeadlessQueue').info(f"HeadlessTaskQueue created (orchestrator will initialize on first use)")
   162→        
   163→        # Task management
   164→        self.task_queue = queue.PriorityQueue()
   165→        self.task_history: Dict[str, GenerationTask] = {}
   166→        self.current_task: Optional[GenerationTask] = None
   167→        self.current_model: Optional[str] = None
   168→        
   169→        # Threading
   170→        self.worker_threads: List[threading.Thread] = []
   171→        self.queue_lock = threading.RLock()
   172→        self.shutdown_event = threading.Event()
   173→        
   174→        # Statistics
   175→        self.stats = {
   176→            "tasks_submitted": 0,
   177→            "tasks_completed": 0,
   178→            "tasks_failed": 0,
   179→            "model_switches": 0,
   180→            "total_generation_time": 0.0
   181→        }
   182→        
   183→        # Setup logging
   184→        self._setup_logging()
   185→        
   186→        # Initialize wgp state (reuse existing state management)
   187→        self._init_wgp_integration()
   188→        
   189→        self.logger.info(f"HeadlessTaskQueue initialized with WanGP at {wan_dir}")
   190→    
   191→    def _setup_logging(self):
   192→        """Setup structured logging that goes to Supabase via the log interceptor."""
   193→        # Keep Python's basic logging for local file backup
   194→        logging.basicConfig(
   195→            level=logging.INFO,
   196→            format='%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(name)s: %(message)s',
   197→            handlers=[
   198→                logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout),
   199→                logging.FileHandler('headless.log')
   200→            ]
   201→        )
   202→        self._file_logger = logging.getLogger('HeadlessQueue')
   203→        
   204→        # Use queue_logger (ComponentLogger) as main logger - this goes to Supabase
   205→        # ComponentLogger has compatible interface: .info(), .error(), .warning(), .debug()
   206→        self.logger = queue_logger
   207→    
   208→    def get_task_status(self, task_id: str) -> Optional[GenerationTask]:
   209→        """Get status of a specific task."""
   210→        return self.task_history.get(task_id)
   211→
   212→    def wait_for_completion(self, task_id: str, timeout: float = 300.0) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   213→        """
   214→        Wait for a task to complete and return the result.
   215→
   216→        Args:
   217→            task_id: ID of the task to wait for
   218→            timeout: Maximum time to wait in seconds
   219→
   220→        Returns:
   221→            Dictionary with 'success', 'output_path', and optional 'error' keys
   222→        """
   223→        start_time = time.time()
   224→
   225→        while (time.time() - start_time) < timeout:
   226→            task_status = self.get_task_status(task_id)
   227→
   228→            if task_status is None:
   229→                return {
   230→                    "success": False,
   231→                    "error": f"Task {task_id} not found in queue"
   232→                }
   233→
   234→            if task_status.status == "completed":
   235→                return {
   236→                    "success": True,
   237→                    "output_path": task_status.result_path
   238→                }
   239→            elif task_status.status == "failed":
   240→                return {
   241→                    "success": False,
   242→                    "error": task_status.error_message or "Task failed with unknown error"
   243→                }
   244→
   245→            # Task is still pending or processing, wait a bit
   246→            time.sleep(1.0)
   247→
   248→        # Timeout reached
   249→        return {
   250→            "success": False,
   251→            "error": f"Task {task_id} did not complete within {timeout} seconds"
   252→        }
   253→
   254→    def get_queue_status(self) -> QueueStatus:
   255→        """Get current queue status."""
   256→        with self.queue_lock:
   257→            return QueueStatus(
   258→                pending_tasks=self.task_queue.qsize(),
   259→                processing_task=self.current_task.id if self.current_task else None,
   260→                completed_tasks=self.stats["tasks_completed"],
   261→                failed_tasks=self.stats["tasks_failed"],
   262→                current_model=self.current_model,
   263→                uptime=time.time() - self.start_time,
   264→                memory_usage=self._get_memory_usage()
   265→            )
   266→
   267→    def _get_memory_usage(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
   268→        """Get current memory usage statistics. Returns stub data for now."""
   269→        return {
   270→            "gpu_memory_used": 0,
   271→            "gpu_memory_total": 0,
   272→            "system_memory_used": 0,
   273→            "model_memory_usage": 0
   274→        }
   275→
   276→    def _cleanup_memory_after_task(self, task_id: str):
   277→        """Clean up memory after task completion WITHOUT unloading models."""
   278→        return cleanup_memory_after_task(self, task_id)
   279→    
   280→    def start(self, preload_model: Optional[str] = None):
   281→        """Start the task queue processing service."""
   282→        return start_queue(self, preload_model=preload_model)
   283→    
   284→    def stop(self, timeout: float = 30.0):
   285→        """Stop the task queue processing service."""
   286→        return stop_queue(self, timeout=timeout)
   287→    
   288→    def submit_task(self, task: GenerationTask) -> str:
   289→        """Submit a new generation task to the queue."""
   290→        return submit_task_impl(self, task)
   291→    
   292→    def _worker_loop(self):
   293→        """Main worker loop for processing tasks."""
   294→        return worker_loop(self)
   295→    
   296→    def _process_task(self, task: GenerationTask, worker_name: str):
   297→        """Process a single generation task."""
   298→        return process_task_impl(self, task, worker_name)
   299→    
   300→    def _switch_model(self, model_key: str, worker_name: str) -> bool:
   301→        """Ensure the correct model is loaded using wgp.py's model management."""
   302→        return switch_model_impl(self, model_key, worker_name)
   303→    
   304→    def _execute_generation(self, task: GenerationTask, worker_name: str) -> str:
   305→        """Execute the actual generation using headless_wgp.py."""
   306→        return execute_generation_impl(self, task, worker_name)

   308→    def _model_supports_vace(self, model_key: str) -> bool:
   309→        """
   310→        Check if a model supports VACE features (video guides, masks, etc.).
   311→        """
   312→        # Ensure orchestrator is initialized before checking model support
   313→        self._ensure_orchestrator()
   314→        
   315→        try:
   316→            # Use orchestrator's VACE detection with model key
   317→            if hasattr(self.orchestrator, 'is_model_vace'):
   318→                return self.orchestrator.is_model_vace(model_key)
   319→            elif hasattr(self.orchestrator, '_is_vace'):
   320→                # Fallback: load model and check (less efficient)
   321→                current_model = self.current_model
   322→                if current_model != model_key:
   323→                    # Would need to load model to check - use name-based detection as fallback
   324→                    return "vace" in model_key.lower()
   325→                return self.orchestrator._is_vace()
   326→            else:
   327→                # Ultimate fallback: name-based detection
   328→                return "vace" in model_key.lower()
   329→        except (AttributeError, ValueError, TypeError) as e:
   330→            self.logger.warning(f"Could not determine VACE support for model '{model_key}': {e}")
   331→            return "vace" in model_key.lower()
   332→    
   333→    def _is_single_image_task(self, task: GenerationTask) -> bool:
   334→        """
   335→        Check if this is a single image task that should be converted from video to PNG.
   336→        """
   337→        # Check if video_length is 1 (single frame) and this looks like an image task
   338→        video_length = task.parameters.get("video_length", 0)
   339→        return video_length == 1
   340→    
   341→    def _convert_single_frame_video_to_png(self, task: GenerationTask, video_path: str, worker_name: str) -> str:
   342→        """
   343→        Convert a single-frame video to PNG format for single image tasks.
   344→        
   345→        This restores the functionality that was in the original single_image.py handler
   346→        where single-frame videos were converted to PNG files.
   347→        """
   348→        try:
   349→            import cv2
   350→            
   351→            video_path_obj = Path(video_path)
   352→            if not video_path_obj.exists():
   353→                self.logger.error(f"Video file does not exist for PNG conversion: {video_path}")
   354→                return video_path  # Return original path if conversion fails
   355→            
   356→            # Create PNG output path with sanitized filename to prevent upload issues
   357→            original_filename = video_path_obj.stem
   358→            
   359→            # Sanitize the filename for storage compatibility
   360→            try:
   361→                from source.utils import sanitize_filename_for_storage
   362→
   363→                sanitized_filename = sanitize_filename_for_storage(original_filename)
   364→                if not sanitized_filename:
   365→                    sanitized_filename = "generated_image"
   366→
   367→            except ImportError:
   368→                # Fallback sanitization if import fails
   369→                import re
   370→                sanitized_filename = re.sub(r'[§®©™@·º½¾¿¡~\x00-\x1F\x7F-\x9F<>:"/\\|?*,]', '', original_filename)
   371→                sanitized_filename = re.sub(r'\s+', '_', sanitized_filename.strip())
   372→                if not sanitized_filename:
   373→                    sanitized_filename = "generated_image"
   374→            
   375→            # Create PNG path with sanitized filename
   376→            png_path = video_path_obj.parent / f"{sanitized_filename}.png"
   377→            
   378→            # Log sanitization if filename changed
   379→            if sanitized_filename != original_filename:
   380→                self.logger.info(f"[PNG_CONVERSION] Task {task.id}: Sanitized filename '{original_filename}' -> '{sanitized_filename}'")
   381→            
   382→            self.logger.info(f"[PNG_CONVERSION] Task {task.id}: Converting {video_path_obj.name} to {png_path.name}")
   383→            
   384→            # Extract the first frame using OpenCV
   385→            cap = cv2.VideoCapture(str(video_path_obj))
   386→            try:
   387→                if cap.isOpened():
   388→                    ret, frame = cap.read()
   389→                    if ret:
   390→                        # Save the frame as PNG
   391→                        success = cv2.imwrite(str(png_path), frame)
   392→                        if success and png_path.exists():
   393→                            self.logger.info(f"[PNG_CONVERSION] Task {task.id}: Successfully saved PNG to {png_path}")
   394→                            
   395→                            # Clean up the original video file
   396→                            try:
   397→                                video_path_obj.unlink()
   398→                                self.logger.info(f"[PNG_CONVERSION] Task {task.id}: Removed original video file")
   399→                            except OSError as e_cleanup:
   400→                                self.logger.warning(f"[PNG_CONVERSION] Task {task.id}: Could not remove original video: {e_cleanup}")
   401→                            
   402→                            return str(png_path)
   403→                        else:
   404→                            self.logger.error(f"[PNG_CONVERSION] Task {task.id}: Failed to save PNG to {png_path}")
   405→                    else:
   406→                        self.logger.error(f"[PNG_CONVERSION] Task {task.id}: Failed to read frame from video")
   407→                else:
   408→                    self.logger.error(f"[PNG_CONVERSION] Task {task.id}: Failed to open video file")
   409→            finally:
   410→                cap.release()
   411→                
   412→        except ImportError:
   413→            self.logger.warning(f"[PNG_CONVERSION] Task {task.id}: OpenCV not available, keeping video format")
   414→        except (OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as e:
   415→            self.logger.error(f"[PNG_CONVERSION] Task {task.id}: Error during conversion: {e}")
   416→        
   417→        # Return original video path if conversion failed
   418→        return video_path

   429→    def _apply_sampler_cfg_preset(self, model_key: str, sample_solver: str, wgp_params: Dict[str, Any]):
   430→        """Apply sampler-specific CFG and flow_shift settings from model configuration."""
   431→        try:
   432→            # Import WGP to get model definition
   433→            # Protect sys.argv in case wgp hasn't been imported yet
   434→            _saved_argv = sys.argv[:]
   435→            try:
   436→                sys.argv = ["headless_model_management.py"]
   437→                import wgp
   438→            finally:
   439→                sys.argv = _saved_argv
   440→
   441→            model_def = wgp.get_model_def(model_key)
   442→            
   443→            # Check if model has sampler-specific presets
   444→            sampler_presets = model_def.get("sampler_cfg_presets", {})
   445→            if sample_solver in sampler_presets:
   446→                preset = sampler_presets[sample_solver]
   447→                
   448→                # Apply preset settings, but allow task parameters to override
   449→                applied_params = {}
   450→                for param, value in preset.items():
   451→                    if param not in wgp_params:  # Only apply if not explicitly set in task
   452→                        wgp_params[param] = value
   453→                        applied_params[param] = value
   454→                        
   455→                self.logger.info(f"Applied sampler '{sample_solver}' CFG preset: {applied_params}")
   456→            else:
   457→                self.logger.debug(f"No CFG preset found for sampler '{sample_solver}' in model '{model_key}'")
   458→                
   459→        except (ValueError, KeyError, AttributeError, TypeError, ImportError) as e:
   460→            self.logger.warning(f"Failed to apply sampler CFG preset: {e}")
   461→

   473→def main():
   474→    """Main entry point for the headless service."""
   475→    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="WanGP Headless Task Queue")
   476→    parser.add_argument("--wan-dir", required=True, help="Path to WanGP directory")
   477→    parser.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=1, help="Number of worker threads")
   478→    parser.add_argument("--debug", action="store_true", help="Enable debug logging")
   479→
   480→    args = parser.parse_args()
   481→
   482→    if args.debug:
   483→        logging.getLogger().setLevel(logging.DEBUG)
   484→
   485→    # Initialize queue
   486→    task_queue = HeadlessTaskQueue(args.wan_dir, max_workers=args.workers)
   487→
   488→    # Setup signal handlers
   489→    def signal_handler(signum, frame):
   490→        queue_logger.essential("Received shutdown signal, stopping...")
   491→        task_queue.stop()
   492→        sys.exit(0)
   493→
   494→    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, signal_handler)
   495→    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, signal_handler)
   496→
   497→    try:
   498→        # Start services
   499→        task_queue.start()
   500→
   501→        queue_logger.essential(f"Headless queue started")
   502→        queue_logger.essential(f"WanGP directory: {args.wan_dir}")
   503→        queue_logger.essential(f"Workers: {args.workers}")
   504→        queue_logger.essential("Press Ctrl+C to stop...")
   505→
   506→        # Example: Submit some test tasks
   507→        if args.debug:
   508→            queue_logger.debug("Submitting test tasks...")
   509→
   510→            # Test T2V task
   511→            t2v_task = create_sample_task(
   512→                "test-t2v-1",
   513→                "t2v",
   514→                "a mystical forest with glowing trees",
   515→                resolution="1280x720",
   516→                video_length=49,
   517→                seed=42
   518→            )
   519→            task_queue.submit_task(t2v_task)
   520→
   521→        # Keep running until shutdown
   522→        while task_queue.running:
   523→            time.sleep(1.0)
   524→
   525→            # Print periodic status
   526→            if args.debug:
   527→                status = task_queue.get_queue_status()
   528→                queue_logger.debug(f"Queue: {status.pending_tasks} pending, "
   529→                      f"{status.completed_tasks} completed, "
   530→                      f"{status.failed_tasks} failed")
   531→
   532→    except KeyboardInterrupt:
   533→        queue_logger.essential("Shutdown requested by user")
   534→    except Exception as e:
   535→        queue_logger.error(f"Fatal error: {e}")
   536→        raise
   537→    finally:
   538→        task_queue.stop()
   539→
   540→
   541→if __name__ == "__main__":
   542→    main()
   543→

     5→- VACE wrapper for generate_video
     6→- Image loading and media path resolution
     7→- Model type checker functions
     8→- Worker notification and directory verification
     9→"""
    10→

    15→

    21→def notify_worker_model_switch(old_model: Optional[str], new_model: str):
    22→    """
    23→    Notify Supabase edge function that a model switch is about to happen.
    24→
    25→    Called BEFORE the actual model load so the worker status can be updated
    26→    to show it's switching models (which can take 30-60+ seconds).
    27→
    28→    Only fires if WORKER_ID is set (i.e., running in cloud worker context).
    29→    """
    30→    worker_id = os.getenv("WORKER_ID")
    31→    if not worker_id:
    32→        return
    33→
    34→    # Prefer service role; fall back to older env var name if present.
    35→    supabase_key = os.getenv("SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY") or os.getenv("SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY")
    36→    if not supabase_key:
    37→        model_logger.debug("No SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, skipping model switch notification")
    38→        return
    39→
    40→    try:
    41→        import httpx
    42→    except ImportError as e:
    43→        model_logger.warning(f"Failed to notify model switch: {e}")
    44→        return
    45→
    46→    try:
    47→        supabase_url = os.getenv("SUPABASE_URL", "https://[REDACTED]")
    48→        response = httpx.post(
    49→            f"{supabase_url.rstrip('/')}/functions/v1/update-worker-model",
    50→            headers={
    51→                "Authorization": f"Bearer {supabase_key}",
    52→                "Content-Type": "application/json"
    53→            },
    54→            json={
    55→                "worker_id": worker_id,
    56→                # Keep payload minimal to avoid schema mismatches server-side.
    57→                "model": new_model,
    58→            },
    59→            timeout=5.0  # Don't block model loading on this
    60→        )
    61→
    62→        if response.status_code == 200:
    63→            model_logger.debug(f"Notified edge function of model switch: {old_model} → {new_model}")
    64→        else:
    65→            model_logger.warning(f"Edge function returned {response.status_code}: {response.text[:200]}")
    66→
    67→    except (httpx.HTTPError, OSError, ValueError) as e:
    68→        # Don't let notification failures block model loading
    69→        model_logger.warning(f"Failed to notify model switch: {e}")
    70→
    71→
    72→def verify_wgp_directory(logger, context: str = ""):
    73→    """
    74→    Verify we're still in the Wan2GP directory after any operation.
    75→
    76→    Wan2GP expects to run from its directory and uses relative paths.
    77→    Call this after any wgp operation to catch directory changes early.
    78→
    79→    Args:
    80→        logger: Logger instance to use

1→"""
     2→Queue lifecycle management extracted from HeadlessTaskQueue.
     3→
     4→Contains start, stop, and submit_task logic.  Every public function takes the
     5→``HeadlessTaskQueue`` instance (aliased *queue*) as its first argument.
     6→"""
     7→
     8→from __future__ import annotations
     9→
    10→import threading
    11→import time
    12→import traceback
    13→from typing import Any
    14→
    15→from source.task_handlers.queue.task_processor import worker_loop, _monitor_loop
    16→
    17→
    18→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    19→# Start
    20→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    21→
    22→def start_queue(queue: Any, preload_model=None):
    23→    """
    24→    Start the task queue processing service.
    25→
    26→    Args:
    27→        queue: The HeadlessTaskQueue instance
    28→        preload_model: Optional model to pre-load before processing tasks.
    29→                      If specified, the model will be loaded immediately after
    30→                      workers start, making the first task much faster.
    31→                      Example: "wan_2_2_vace_lightning_baseline_2_2_2"
    32→    """
    33→    if queue.running:
    34→        queue.logger.warning("Queue already running")
    35→        return
    36→
    37→    queue.running = True
    38→    queue.shutdown_event.clear()
    39→
    40→    # Start worker threads
    41→    for i in range(queue.max_workers):
    42→        worker = threading.Thread(
    43→            target=worker_loop,
    44→            args=(queue,),
    45→            name=f"GenerationWorker-{i}",
    46→            daemon=True
    47→        )
    48→        worker.start()
    49→        queue.worker_threads.append(worker)
    50→
    51→    # Start monitoring thread
    52→    monitor = threading.Thread(
    53→        target=_monitor_loop,
    54→        args=(queue,),
    55→        name="QueueMonitor",
    56→        daemon=True
    57→    )
    58→    monitor.start()
    59→    queue.worker_threads.append(monitor)
    60→
    61→    queue.logger.info(f"Task queue started with {queue.max_workers} workers")
    62→
    63→    # Pre-load model if specified
    64→    if preload_model:
    65→        queue.logger.info(f"Pre-loading model: {preload_model}")
    66→        try:
    67→            # Initialize orchestrator and load model in background
    68→            queue._ensure_orchestrator()
    69→            if queue.orchestrator is None:
    70→                raise RuntimeError("Orchestrator initialization failed during preload")
    71→            queue.orchestrator.load_model(preload_model)
    72→            queue.current_model = preload_model
    73→            queue.logger.info(f"Model {preload_model} pre-loaded successfully")
    74→        except (RuntimeError, ValueError, OSError) as e:
    75→            # Log the full error with traceback
    76→            queue.logger.error(f"FATAL: Failed to pre-load model {preload_model}: {e}\n{traceback.format_exc()}")
    77→
    78→            # If orchestrator failed to initialize, this is fatal - worker cannot function
    79→            if queue.orchestrator is None:
    80→                queue.logger.error("Orchestrator failed to initialize - worker cannot process tasks. Exiting.")
    81→                raise RuntimeError(f"Orchestrator initialization failed during preload: {e}") from e
    82→            else:
    83→                # Orchestrator is OK but model load failed - this is recoverable
    84→                queue.logger.warning(f"Model {preload_model} failed to load, but orchestrator is ready. Worker will continue.")
    85→
    86→
    87→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    88→# Stop
    89→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    90→
    91→def stop_queue(queue: Any, timeout: float = 30.0):
    92→    """Stop the task queue processing service."""
    93→    if not queue.running:
    94→        return
    95→
    96→    queue.logger.info("Shutting down task queue...")
    97→    queue.running = False
    98→    queue.shutdown_event.set()
    99→
   100→    # Wait for workers to finish
   101→    for worker in queue.worker_threads:
   102→        worker.join(timeout=timeout)
   103→
   104→    # Save queue state (integrate with wgp.py's save system)
   105→    queue._save_queue_state()
   106→
   107→    # Optionally unload model to free VRAM
   108→    # queue._cleanup_models()
   109→
   110→    queue.logger.info("Task queue shutdown complete")
   111→
   112→
   113→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   114→# Submit
   115→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   116→
   117→def submit_task_impl(queue: Any, task: Any) -> str:
   118→    """
   119→    Submit a new generation task to the queue.
   120→
   121→    Args:
   122→        queue: The HeadlessTaskQueue instance
   123→        task: Generation task to process
   124→
   125→    Returns:
   126→        Task ID for tracking
   127→    """
   128→    with queue.queue_lock:
   129→        # Pre-validate task conversion (actual conversion happens in _process_task)
   130→        queue._convert_to_wgp_task(task)
   131→
   132→        # Add to queue with priority (higher priority = processed first)
   133→        queue.task_queue.put((-task.priority, time.time(), task))
   134→        queue.task_history[task.id] = task
   135→        queue.stats["tasks_submitted"] += 1
   136→
   137→        queue.logger.info(f"Task submitted: {task.id} (model: {task.model}, priority: {task.priority})")
   138→        return task.id
   139→

    67→def move_wgp_output_to_task_type_dir(output_path: str, task_type: str, task_id: str, main_output_dir_base: Path) -> str:
    68→    """
    69→    Move WGP-generated output from base directory to task-type subdirectory.
    70→
    71→    This function handles post-processing of WGP outputs to organize them by task_type.
    72→    WGP generates all files to a globally-configured base directory, so we move them
    73→    to task-type subdirectories after generation completes.
    74→
    75→    Args:
    76→        output_path: Path to the WGP-generated file (in base directory)
    77→        task_type: Task type (e.g., "vace", "flux", "t2v")
    78→        task_id: Task ID
    79→        main_output_dir_base: Base output directory
    80→
    81→    Returns:
    82→        New path if file was moved, original path otherwise
    83→    """
    84→    # Only process WGP task types
    85→    from source.task_handlers.tasks.task_types import WGP_TASK_TYPES
    86→    if task_type not in WGP_TASK_TYPES:
    87→        return output_path
    88→
    89→    try:
    90→        output_file = Path(output_path)
    91→
    92→        # Check if file exists
    93→        if not output_file.exists():
    94→            headless_logger.debug(f"Output file doesn't exist, skipping move: {output_path}", task_id=task_id)
    95→            return output_path
    96→
    97→        # Check if file is in base directory (not already in a subdirectory)
    98→        # If the parent directory is main_output_dir_base, it's in base directory
    99→        if output_file.parent.resolve() != main_output_dir_base.resolve():
   100→            headless_logger.debug(f"Output already in subdirectory, skipping move: {output_path}", task_id=task_id)
   101→            return output_path
   102→
   103→        # Generate new path in task-type subdirectory
   104→        filename = output_file.name
   105→        new_path, _ = prepare_output_path(
   106→            task_id=task_id,
   107→            filename=filename,
   108→            main_output_dir_base=main_output_dir_base,
   109→            task_type=task_type
   110→        )
   111→
   112→        # Move the file
   113→        headless_logger.info(
   114→            f"Moving WGP output to task-type directory: {output_file} → {new_path} (task_type={task_type})",
   115→            task_id=task_id
   116→        )
   117→
   118→        # Ensure destination directory exists
   119→        new_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   120→
   121→        # Move the file
   122→        shutil.move(str(output_file), str(new_path))
   123→
   124→        headless_logger.success(f"Moved WGP output to {new_path}", task_id=task_id)
   125→        return str(new_path)
   126→
   127→    except (OSError, shutil.Error, ValueError) as e:
   128→        headless_logger.error(f"Failed to move WGP output to task-type directory: {e}", task_id=task_id, exc_info=True)
   129→        # Return original path if move fails
   130→        return output_path

     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import os

     8→from contextlib import contextmanager
     9→from dataclasses import dataclass
    10→from pathlib import Path
    11→from typing import Any, Callable, Iterator
    12→
    13→_BOOTSTRAP_STATE: dict[tuple[str | None, str], dict[str, Any]] = {}
    14→_RUNTIME_CONTEXTS: dict[str, list["RuntimeContext"]] = {}

    17→def _normalize_path(value: str | os.PathLike[str] | None) -> str | None:
    18→    if value is None:
    19→        return None
    20→    return str(Path(value).resolve())
    21→
    22→
    23→def apply_process_globals(
    24→    *,
    25→    cwd: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None,
    26→    argv: list[str] | None = None,
    27→    prepend_sys_path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None,
    28→) -> None:
    29→    """Persistently update process-global execution state."""
    30→    if cwd is not None:
    31→        os.chdir(_normalize_path(cwd))
    32→    if argv is not None:
    33→        sys.argv = list(argv)
    34→    if prepend_sys_path is not None:
    35→        path = _normalize_path(prepend_sys_path)
    36→        if path is not None:
    37→            try:
    38→                sys.path.remove(path)
    39→            except ValueError:
    40→                pass
    41→            sys.path.insert(0, path)
    42→
    43→
    44→@contextmanager
    45→def temporary_process_globals(
    46→    *,
    47→    cwd: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None,
    48→    argv: list[str] | None = None,
    49→    prepend_sys_path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None,
    50→) -> Iterator[None]:
    51→    """Temporarily apply process-global state and restore it afterwards."""
    52→    original_cwd = os.getcwd()
    53→    original_argv = list(sys.argv)
    54→    original_sys_path = list(sys.path)
    55→    try:
    56→        apply_process_globals(cwd=cwd, argv=argv, prepend_sys_path=prepend_sys_path)
    57→        yield
    58→    finally:
    59→        os.chdir(original_cwd)
    60→        sys.argv = original_argv
    61→        sys.path[:] = original_sys_path
    62→
    63→

    65→    return context_id
    66→
    67→

    71→

    77→    name: str,

    86→    state_key = (controller, name)

    88→    if state is not None and state.get("version") == version:

    90→
    91→    initializer()
    92→    new_state = {
    93→        "name": name,
    94→        "version": version,
    95→        "metadata": metadata or {},
    96→        "controller": controller,
    97→        "context_id": context_id,
    98→        "last_ran_at": time.time(),
    99→    }
   100→    _BOOTSTRAP_STATE[state_key] = new_state
   101→    return new_state

   104→@dataclass
   105→class RuntimeContext:
   106→    """Prepared runtime execution scope."""
   107→
   108→    name: str
   109→    wan_root: str
   110→    default_argv: list[str]
   111→    require_cwd: bool
   112→
   113→    def prepare(
   114→        self,
   115→        *,
   116→        argv: list[str] | None = None,
   117→        require_cwd: bool | None = None,
   118→    ) -> None:
   119→        effective_require_cwd = self.require_cwd if require_cwd is None else require_cwd
   120→        apply_process_globals(
   121→            cwd=self.wan_root if effective_require_cwd else None,
   122→            argv=argv or self.default_argv,
   123→            prepend_sys_path=self.wan_root,
   124→        )
   125→
   126→    @contextmanager
   127→    def scoped(
   128→        self,
   129→        *,
   130→        argv: list[str] | None = None,
   131→        cwd: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None,
   132→        require_cwd: bool | None = None,
   133→    ) -> Iterator[None]:
   134→        effective_require_cwd = self.require_cwd if require_cwd is None else require_cwd
   135→        with temporary_process_globals(
   136→            cwd=cwd or (self.wan_root if effective_require_cwd else None),
   137→            argv=argv or self.default_argv,
   138→            prepend_sys_path=self.wan_root,
   139→        ):
   140→            yield
   141→
   142→
   143→def get_runtime_context(
   144→    name: str,
   145→    *,
   146→    wan_root: str | os.PathLike[str],
   147→    default_argv: list[str],
   148→    require_cwd: bool,
   149→) -> RuntimeContext:
   150→    context = RuntimeContext(
   151→        name=name,
   152→        wan_root=_normalize_path(wan_root) or "",
   153→        default_argv=list(default_argv),
   154→        require_cwd=require_cwd,
   155→    )
   156→    _RUNTIME_CONTEXTS.setdefault(name, []).append(context)
   157→    return context
   158→
   159→
   160→def reset_runtime_contexts(name: str | None = None) -> None:
   161→    if name is None:

   174→        cwd=wan_root if require_cwd else None,
   175→        argv=argv,

1→"""
     2→WGP/CUDA initialization mixin for HeadlessTaskQueue.
     3→
     4→Handles CUDA warmup, diagnostics, and lazy WanOrchestrator initialization.
     5→Separated from the main queue coordinator to isolate the complex
     6→startup/initialization logic.
     7→"""
     8→
     9→import os
    10→import sys
    11→import time
    12→import traceback
    13→from dataclasses import dataclass
    14→
    15→from source.core.log import is_debug_enabled
    16→from source.runtime.process_globals import get_runtime_context, temporary_process_globals
